| B43 | **Undo history** (human, 2026-08-24). Wanted; not yet designed. The hard parts are specific to THIS instrument and are recorded so a future session does not discover them one at a time. **(a) One gesture is not one parameter.** A morph XY move rewrites every owned parameter at once (222 owners today), a corner CAPTURE writes a whole patch, a preset load replaces everything, and an atomic group flips as a unit (ADR-109 A1: root + 12 scale degrees). So the undo unit is a COMMAND, not a param write — a per-param log would make one XY nudge cost 222 undo steps and be useless. **(b) Snapshots are the obvious design and the wrong one.** The global doctrine records that a large state chunk makes hosts silently fail to save; a ring of full-state snapshots is exactly that failure waiting, and it must not touch `getStateInformation` at all. Store deltas (id -> before/after) with a bounded ring, and keep undo state OUT of the saved chunk unless the human explicitly wants history to survive a session. **(c) Who owns it — GUI or shell?** GUI-side is far cheaper and can ship first, but dies with the window and cannot see edits arriving from host automation. Shell-side sees everything but sits next to the RT thread, where the no-allocation rule applies — a growing history is exactly the allocation that rule forbids, so it needs preallocation and a fixed cap. **(d) Host automation is the genuine conflict, and it is a RULING not a bug**: if the host is automating a parameter, an undo that rewrites it either fights the automation or is instantly overwritten. Decide up front whether automated parameters are excluded from history, or whether undo is refused while transport is rolling. **(e) The gesture latch is already there to reuse** — `bridge.gesture(id, on)` already brackets every knob drag (ADR-121), so 'one drag = one undo step' needs no new plumbing, only a listener. Related: B35's randomize-a-corner is a one-way door until this exists, which is why that entry pairs it with an initialize button; undo would make the pairing unnecessary | § ADR-109 · § ADR-121 · § B35 |
| B42 | **DISCUSSION, not committed — lower the voice cap, and/or replace osc 2 with offset LAYERS** (human, 2026-08-24: *"my research is showing me that supersaws actually lose audible power after as few as 8 voices"* … *"a second and possibly third layer with offset values on relevant parameters instead of full editability for each"* … *"I'm not committed to this turn yet, but it's worth discussing the trade-offs"*). **THE VOICE CAP. The case for is strong and specific: the over-budget case IS the voice ceiling.** `{1, "n", "Voices", 1, 32, 7}` (`hypersaw_clap.cpp:133`) allows 32, and cost is linear in the inner voice loop, so 32v x 16n measures 16.23% = **64.9% derated, over the 50% budget**, while a cap of 12 would put the same worst case near 6% = ~24% derated. One parameter-range change would close the headroom gap the B41 audit opened. **Three arguments against acting on the literature alone.** (a) **The supersaw research is about STATIC detuned stacks; this is not one.** SWARM SAW is a coupled Kuramoto system: at high K the voices LOCK (more voices add level, not width) and at low K they splay and drift, so the saturation point is an empirical property of THIS engine at a given K, not an inherited constant. It is also cheap to settle — an A/B render at 8 / 16 / 32 voices across several K values, which we have the tooling for and have never run. (b) **Six golden scenarios use n > 12** (one at 32, two at 24, three at 16 — `tools/golden/gen_goldens.mjs`), so lowering the max is a parity-breaking reference change needing an ADR, never an optimisation commit. (c) Existing patches above the new max would clamp silently, and a CLAP range change can strand host automation. **Middle paths worth weighing before a hard cap:** move the DEFAULT rather than the max; make the ceiling CPU-budget-aware rather than a fixed range; or cap per-oscillator so 2 slots x 32 cannot both be spent. **THE LAYERS QUESTION, and the honest headline: offset layers do NOT save CPU.** A layer still renders its own voices, and the measured 1.8-2.0x cost of oscillator 2 IS the voice loop — offsets change what you can EDIT, not what gets computed. What they genuinely save is **parameter surface**: each full slot is ~60 params at OSC_STRIDE 1000, against perhaps 8-12 offsets, which compounds into preset size, the morph field (222 owners today) and every UI page. That is a real and large win, just not a CPU one — and worth wanting for its own sake. **The version that WOULD pay in CPU is a different architecture and should not be confused with this one:** one shared voice bank with multiple output taps, so a two-layer sound renders one swarm rather than two. That halves the voice loop where offset-layers halve only the parameter count. Cost of layers: an offset cannot express a layer in a different topology or mode, so it trades range for simplicity — acceptable for a 3rd layer, contentious for the 2nd | § B41 · § B18b · § ADR-082 |

| B124 | **Stale corner slots across loads — "semi-permanently messes up that corner until I reload the plugin"** (human 2026-09-14, reported as a history bug). Headless repro through undo was clean; the real mechanism is in the LOADERS: a stored corner/exempt array SHORTER than the live order only overwrote the slots it carried, so the previous load's values survived in the rest. The human's files mix 224-entry (Dreamfield, Examples 1/2, FX - Blegh), 222-entry (power hour, Lifeslop, most corner presets) and 202-entry (LD - Happy Days, Ascend, Cello 1) arrays — so a pitch offset (181/1181) from a recent preset, or the whole bend/note-law/globals/scale tail after a 202-entry file, outlived every later load, and only a plugin reload (fresh defaults) cleared it. History made it VISIBLE (a restore is a full 224 snapshot; the next short load re-mixed) but did not cause it. **Fix (PR pending):** `resetCorner(k)` to each slot's `defaultFor` before filling, in both `applyMorphChunk` (corners; exempt → 0) and `cornerApply`; `cornerMatches` treats uncarried slots as "must read default" so the asterisk agrees. `morphlayout_check` T8a–c (224 → 222 corner preset resets 181/1181; 224 → 222 patch resets too). Open: the headless probe printed the node count one below the expected after a load — worth a look next beat, not a shipping issue | § ADR-159 · § B122 · § B84 |
| B125 | **A load rewrote the corners — "a reverted corner might become whatever the corner A preset is"** (human 2026-09-14, after B124; "a few times it doesn't seem like a corner preset was actually saved to history"). ROOT CAUSE, reproduced by `morphlayout_check` T9 (fails with the bypass disabled, passes with it): every parameter write passes the ADR-109 choke point, which with morph ON routes a write into a corner — the ARMED one, the winning one (quantum) or all four weighted (blend). A STATE LOAD (preset, history restore, host chunk) enqueues every parameter; the morph chunk sets the corners synchronously, then the queued writes drain on the audio thread and are routed into the corners as if they were edits — so the corners take the loaded state's LIVE values, which with the pad parked on A are corner A's. It happened "not always" because it needs morph on and depends on mode, arm and pad position. **Fix (PR pending):** queue kind 3 = a load's value; `loadingState` is set for the duration of each such write (and around the host chunk's direct writes) and `morphRouteEdit` treats it as a plain live write; the GUI's edits (kind 0) route exactly as before. B124's stale-slot fix stands as a second, independent cause. The "not saved to history" part: unverified — the headless tree was correct in every probe; the human's own observation of the row is the next evidence | § ADR-109 · § B124 · § B84 |

The 2026-08-06 `dist/cpu_bench` had a `__data` section of 0 bytes; the rebuild at `6585db9` has 1 310 808 bytes there (`size -m`), the whole binary 186 KB → 2.80 MB, while `__text` moved only 31.9 → 42.3 KB. The bench's only large object is `hypersaw::SwarmCore`, which it constructs on the STACK (`tools/cpu_bench.cpp:33`) and whose `sizeof` is 667 456 bytes today against 667 032 forty commits ago — so it is NOT the core object and NOT a member array. A non-zero-initialised global or function-static of ~1.3 MB in `src/swarm_core.h` or a header it includes; the shipped plugin compiles the same header, so the bundle likely carries it too. Investigate: `nm -m --size-sort` on the bench, `size -m` on the installed `horde.clap`; whether it belongs in `__const` (a table that should be `constexpr`/`static const` → `__TEXT`), in `__bss` (zero-init), or is a cache that should live on the instance. Cheap, and the class (a table in the wrong section) is one the auditor's cost sweep should learn to see. | for the auditor's next sweep, or a 20-minute scout |
| B164 | **Macros: spring-to-origin and polarity as per-macro options; the bend axis springs now** (human 2026-09-19: "Bend should spring to center; I think all macros should have the option of springing to origin in general (and macros should be settable to unipolar or bipolar)"). Two halves. (a) BUILT NOW: a MAIN pad axis assigned to Pitch Bend writes the bend target back to 0 on release through the same path the drag used, so the bend travel law (param 106) carries the return like a released wheel; Pad Latch (268) holds it; a macro axis and the Mod Wheel axis are untouched. **BUILT 2026-09-19 → PR #681** (verify full exit 0 on `9145d95`; leak gate clean): GUI-side only — `padSpringRelease()` on pointerup writes the bend target 0 through the drag's own three lines, so param 106's law carries the return; Pad Latch (268) is the opt-out; macro / Mod Wheel / None / the OSC pad early-out; `padPuck` reads the live param so it follows the return. FINDING, for B164(b): TWO SURFACES, TWO SPRINGS, ONE PARAMETER — the Wheel strip springs to its PRE-GESTURE value (ADR-112: a corner may hold a non-zero Pitch and a wheel that springs to zero would stomp it) while the pad now springs to 0, so a patch whose corner holds Pitch +1 st loses it on pad release; the ruling's absolute geometry forces this today, and the origin-editor (B170) is where both surfaces should agree on what 'origin' means. Also: no post-law bend readback exists shell→GUI, so the puck SNAPS while the sound travels (a readout is a small shell addition when wanted); `pointercancel` on the pad is unhandled (pre-existing). (b) DESIGN, for the intent-bus GUI batch (B170): per-macro `spring` (return to its ORIGIN on release — origin = the corner-owned rest position under the bus, SPEC-INTENT-BUS §5, or the macro's default off the bus) and per-macro `polarity` {unipolar 0..1, bipolar ±1 about the origin}; a spring is a performance property (Device class, like 268), polarity changes what the knob's travel MEANS to every binding and route, so it is patch state. B134 already put polarity on the ROUTE — a per-macro polarity is the SOURCE's declared polarity, which B134's table reads, so the two compose rather than compete. Not built until the bus's home/origin editor exists (B170), or the spring has nowhere visible to return to. | § ADR-150 · § ADR-176 · § B134 · § B170 |
| B165 | **Macro presets — a saveable list of macro settings inside a patch, with a glide time between them** (human 2026-09-19: "A 'macro presets' list section (part of a global preset) where you can save and load macro settings, and also set a glide time so the switch between macro presets doesn't have to be continuous"). Shape: a patch carries N named snapshots of the eight macro values (+ the pad); selecting one glides every macro to the snapshot over a patch-level `macroGlide` seconds (0 = jump), through the ordinary macro write path so every binding and route follows; a snapshot is the natural target for a MIDI program-change or a step of a sequencer. Under the bus a snapshot is a vector in intent space, so it composes with the corners. Sequencing: after B170 (the macros must first mean something under morph). | § B89 · § B170 |

| B170 | **Intent bus phase 3 — the bus becomes visible and usable** (the human's review 2026-09-19 after listening with the flag on: "all that's here is the name changes to the macro, which aren't editable as they ultimately should be, the center ring on the Main XY which also isn't repositionable per corner, nor is there a setting to make the XY spring back to it as in the lab. I don't know what pad latch means. And macros are still turned off when morph is turned on, so the Main XY becomes useless"). The review is CORRECT and the lead's record should have said so before the human found it: phases 2a–2d built the RESOLVER behind a flag with the prototype as its parity oracle, and NOTHING of §5's UI — the plan (`docs/proposals/b89-phase2-intent-resolver.md`) put the pickers, the pad, and the corner-scope routings in phase 3. What the shell already holds, invisible: per-corner HOMES (`intentHomeX/Y[4]`, chunk `H:k:x:y`), per-patch intent NAMES (the chunk carries renames; only the defaults are ever shown), the SPRING (Pad Latch 268 OFF = the puck springs to the owning corner's home — the default — ON = it stays; the name is the spec's word, it should read 'Pad spring' with the polarity flipped), and bind tables per corner (empty by default). Two defects the review exposes: (1) the spring moves the PUCK (the X/Y intents) but the pad DRAWS the two macro parameters (the pointer, which the shell never writes — ADR-176's 'the shell writes neither'), and those two macros also feed their own M-intents, so the visible position does not return and half the pad's effect does not either — the pointer/puck split has to be resolved in the GUI (draw the puck; on release, the pad's macros follow the puck through the ordinary write path unless latched); (2) with the flag on, macros are still suspended under morph (`macroLive`, ADR-152) and the corners have no bindings, so a macro reaches nothing — the bus was meant to RETIRE the suspension: with the flag on, the macro family's routes must stay live (the corner-range clamp is the safety, §4.5) and every corner ships a default bind table (identity: macro N → its assigned parameters at the corner's range) so a knob does something before anyone edits. BUILD (one batch, GUI-heavy, the lab `reference/intent-bus.html` is the reference for every affordance): (a) names editable (double-click the label; per patch, as stored); (b) a home editor on the MAIN pad — drag the ring per corner, 'set home = here', shown in the corner's colour; (c) Pad Latch → 'Pad spring' with clear copy; the puck drawn, the spring visible, the pad's macros following the puck on release (B164(a)'s bend spring is the same gesture on a different target); (d) the suspension retired under the flag + default bind tables; (e) the binding editor: per corner, intent → parameter → range, with B167's right-click 'map to' as its entry gesture and B169's range drag on the destination; (f) B164(b) per-macro spring/polarity; (g) B168 double-click-to-origin. ACCEPTANCE (to be written per item before dispatch): parity with the lab's behaviours where the lab has them (T3/T7/T8 pad rows of §12), `intent_check` extended, no new parameter ids beyond the per-macro spring/polarity if they are params. | § ADR-152 · § ADR-176 · § B89 · § B164 · § B167 · § B168 · § B169 |

Sub should have its own mono toggle, with 'lowest' as the MIDI bias and a simple glide knob. 3. Sub needs a visualizer to see the shape. 4. Sub needs one of its pitch parameters to also be mappable smoothly to a pitch envelope. 5. Sub needs to be on the mix page. 6. Sub currently seems to be ignored by loading presets"). Dispatched 2026-09-20 as one item (branch `subosc-six-notes`); the request sanctions the protected edits note 1 needs. **(1)** octave −2..0 → reaching −3, in the core table, the lab's select and SPEC-SUBOSC §7 together so parity holds; default stays −1 so patches are bit-inert. **(2)** mono / bias 'lowest' / glide built SHELL-side (voice assignment and glide are the shell's job for the swarm too; the sub's core stays a single-voice renderer), new ids above 4015 in the block, defaults bit-inert. **(3)** a wave display that must NOT become a third copy of a shape law — either the shell publishes the cycle (the existing bind idiom) or a check asserts the two laws agree, because B177 already left one such copy and it is this repo's named failure mode. **(4)** verify first whether `fine`/`semis` are ALREADY mod destinations (the 4000 block is not in the refusal range) — if so the gap is RANGE, not capability, since ±100 cents is one semitone; preferred fix is a dedicated continuous semitone offset rather than moving `fine`'s meaning, which is also the shape B180 proposes instrument-wide. **(5)** a MIX strip surfacing the SAME level id (B166's rule). **(6) IS A REAL DEFECT AND WIDER THAN THE SUB, confirmed in the code by the lead:** `applyStateJson` skips any key absent from the loaded patch (`if (pos == npos) continue;`), so that parameter keeps whatever it currently holds. The engine-block loop even defends it — 'a patch written before the block existed simply says nothing about it, and the block ships off, so it stays inert' — whose hidden assumption fails the moment the user turns the block ON: it then persists across every preset load, which is exactly what the human heard. **The same function applies the OPPOSITE rule three lines above**, to routes and to the intent chunk: 'a load is a load — an ABSENT key means unbound … never whatever the previous patch had'. Fixed in favour of a load is a load: an absent parameter restores to its DEFAULT. Evidence required: all 40 factory patches load byte-identically after every parameter is deliberately disturbed, with a control proving a named key still restores its own value. ACCEPTANCE: verify full green; parity green after the golden regeneration; each note's bit-inertness control; the visualizer proven to agree with the sound; a routed envelope measurably moving the sub's pitch; screenshots of the SUB panel and MIX. **BUILT 2026-09-20 → PR #699** (verify full exit 0 on `1f57ef4`; leak gate clean; seven commits, one per note plus a pin): (1) the octave floor reaches −3 in the three places that are ONE fact — core table, lab, spec — default unchanged so the widening is bit-inert, with absolute-value coverage added at the new floor; (2) mono / bias `lowest` / glide built SHELL-side, the core gaining only a `pitchOffsetSt` input rather than a 16th table row, because the block's id map is positional under a frozen gate at 4015; (3) `SubOscCore::shapeAt` EXTRACTED out of `render()`'s inner loop so the shell publishes the very cycle the sound is made from — the deliberate non-repeat of B177's second copy — and parity still reads 0.000e+00, which proves the extraction changed no arithmetic; (4) measurement first confirmed `sub.fine` ALREADY routed and the gap was range, then a dedicated `sub.pitchMod` was wired; (5) a MIX strip on the sub's own ids; (6) the state-load defect fixed — an absent parameter now restores its default. **THE MOST IMPORTANT RESULT IS A CALIBRATION THAT DID NOT FIRE, AND IT INDICTS THE LEAD'S BRIEF:** the 40-patch byte-identity evidence the lead specified for note 6 PASSES ON THE PRE-FIX BINARY — the factory bank has no holes, so skip-and-default agree on it. The proposed evidence was not evidence. Genuinely red-pre-fix rows were added in its place and the boundary recorded (L0033, and now L0059). A RED intermediate run was reported rather than buried: `intent_check` T4's control failed because its seed search picked a seed on the CENTRE alone and assumed the off-centre control would split too — appending two morphable ids lengthens `morphIds`, and `MorphField::reshuffle` draws the SHARED gumbel AFTER every per-parameter draw, so a longer list shifts it and re-decides ownership wherever `morphCoup > 0`. **`src/morph_core.h` was NOT touched** (the lead verified): only the check's search widened, with the reason written at the pin. The user-facing consequence belongs to B175's family — appending morphable parameters can move corner ownership on an existing patch when coupling is on; it reaches audio only under the intent-bus flag, which ships off. | B187 | **~~`o1.tilt` loses every value above 1 to the `toneTilt` alias~~ — THE LEAD'S RECORDED CAUSE WAS WRONG; the real defect is a raw-id test where a base-id test belongs** (found by B186's gauntlet, 2026-09-20). **CORRECTED 2026-09-22 by the agent sent to fix it, which refused and produced the evidence instead — the row said 'an alias with a different range' and there is NO alias.** Id 45 `tilt` is SPECTRA's roll-off EXPONENT (`amp[k] = 1/pow(k+1, tilt)`, range 0.5..2) and id 71 `toneTilt` is SWARM's BIPOLAR tilt whose sign selects high-pass from low-pass (range −1..1): two different parameters, on two different cores, deliberately different, and the code says so in three places. **The real defect:** `applyParam`'s SPECTRA branch tests the RAW id while `readParam`'s tests the BASE id, so the twin 1045 falls through and ALSO writes `cores[1].setParam("tilt")` — one control silently driving two unrelated parameters on two engines. Gated behind a gauntlet exclusion that goes RED once fixed, so the exclusion cannot outlive the bug, with a control (id 45, the same Amp Tilt on oscillator 1, DOES round-trip) proving the probe is not indiscriminate. **RAISED 2026-09-20 by B174, and CONFIRMED by measurement 2026-09-22:** the new global dirty predicate compares the patch against its preset, so a parameter the loader CLAMPS never matches — a player loading any preset that stores `o1.tilt` above 1 sees a spurious asterisk that cannot be cleared. | B191 | **A `<select>` never marks a history node — a whole CLASS of parameters is missing from history, not one control** (human 2026-09-21: "I'm also not certain the sub osc parameters are all wired into history properly (I changed the shape value and it didn't make a node). For a knob that is sound, because the knob wrapper captures the pointer (~2390-2425). For a `<select>` it is not: the native dropdown is a platform popup OUTSIDE the document, so the release commonly never lands on the element, and a keyboard change produces no pointer events at all. The bracket never closes, and no node is made. The sub's Wave is a select — which is exactly what the human saw — and so is every waveform, mode, FX type and the sub's own mono bias. **The sub was the messenger, not the bug.** Build: bracket a DISCRETE control (select, checkbox) around the value CHANGE itself, synchronously, since it has no drag; leave continuous controls their drag bracket; state in one place why pointer events are the wrong signal for a popup-based control so the next control type does not re-derive it; and share the bracket helper rather than leaving two ways of bracketing that must agree. Guard the double-bracket hazard — the knob path's own comment records that an unbalanced gesture is "how a host records automation it can never undo" — by ASSERTING balance per control type. **The real deliverable is the gate:** for EVERY parameter the GUI exposes, changing it through its own control must produce exactly one node, driven from the presentation table so a newly added parameter is covered automatically rather than by someone remembering. Exclusions must be DECLARED in the gate (ADR-160 (3): host events and automation never mark; dev/device toggles may not either) — an exclusion that is merely absent is indistinguishable from a bug. **BUILT 2026-09-21 → PR #706** (verify full exit 0 on `1807cc1` per `.harness/last-verify.json`; leak gate clean). **THE GAP WAS FAR WIDER THAN THE LEAD'S DIAGNOSIS: the pre-fix wiring failed 399 of 874 scenarios across EIGHT interaction classes**, not one. A control whose pointer events are deliberately disabled can never bracket from pointer events. Fix: ONE idempotent `gestureFor(el)` latch per element, cached on the element and remembering the id it opened with; continuous drags keep the pointer bracket, everything else — including a range's keyboard path — brackets around its own value change; `wireKnob`, `resetToDefault`, the M/S buttons and both power buttons now share that latch instead of four hand-rolled ones. Exclusions are DECLARED (`NO_HISTORY_IDS`: 178 specimen, ADR-147) and the gate reads that set OUT OF THE PAGE, asserting the excluded control still writes its parameter and emits ZERO brackets. Three plants — a pointer-only select on its keyboard path, the same select through a native popup, and a control with no bracket at all — each turn the gate red. **THE LEAD WIRED THE GATE ON INTEGRATION, and the reason is a defect in the lead's own boilerplate:** the brief carried a blanket "do not edit `./verify`" beside the instruction to wire new checks, and ADR-180 §1 had already narrowed that gate to WEAKENING — adding is not gated. The agent obeyed the stricter line and said so, which was correct from inside the brief; the contradiction was the lead's. Boilerplate corrected so the next brief does not reproduce it, and the harness header now records the episode instead of the stale `UNWIRED:` marker. TWO THINGS FOR THE HUMAN TO NOTICE IN USE: a range moved by the KEYBOARD now makes one node per arrow press where it made none before, so a held arrow key fills history faster than a drag (there is a `histCoalesce` setting; whether it should cover this is a ruling); and the specimen toggle now emits no host gesture at all where it previously bracketed, which is what being on the exclusion list means. ACCEPTANCE: verify full green; the control-type matrix reported; the sub's Wave produces exactly one node, red before; a planted non-bracketing control type turns the gate red. | § ADR-160 · § B84 · § B186 |

| B202 | **The Sub Osc clicks when notes overlap in mono** (human 2026-09-22: "When the Sub Osc is set to mono, there's a click artifact when notes overlap"). The sub's core REPLACES the sounding note rather than layering it (`src/subosc_core.h`'s header states it), so the overlap path is where a new note arrives while the old one still sounds, and the click is somewhere in that handover. Three candidates and the fix depends on which: a phase reset, an envelope restart, or a glide target jump. **Not to be conflated with a DIFFERENT discontinuity already on record** — B181 note 2 left the block silencing when the mono TOGGLE crosses, which is deliberate and awaits its own ruling; the brief requires each measurement to say which one it is hearing. Gated by MEASUREMENT rather than by ear: a click is a sample-to-sample discontinuity, so the maximum step across the overlap instant is asserted against a bound derived from the signal's own natural slope — the shape `tools/station_check.cpp` already uses ("N× the natural step"), with the control showing the bound exceeded before the fix. **BUILT 2026-09-22 → PR #717** (verify full exit 0 on `38c06e5`; leak gate clean). **The cause was FOUND before anything was changed, and two candidates were eliminated rather than assumed:** `subStruckKey` is cleared when the last key lifts, so the next press STRIKES rather than glides; `SubOscCore::noteOn` replaces the sounding note; and with `release` at 0.08 s the previous note's tail is still live, so the PHASE RESET underneath it is the click. The envelope was ruled out by construction (it continues, it does not restart) and the glide likewise (it moves the increment, not the value), with velocity held constant to keep them separable. Fix: reuse `SwarmCore::retargetNote`'s existing `keepPhase` word on `SubOscCore::noteOn`, defaulting FALSE so parity is untouched, passed true only when `env > 0`. **Measured 18.18× the signal's natural step before, 1.44× after** (gate at 2×, worst of 16 phases 21.50× → 1.80×). The deliberate mono-TOGGLE discontinuity is the must-step CONTROL at 20.87×, which keeps the two distinct by construction rather than by care. | § B181 · § B172 · § ADR-099 |
| B203 | **The sub's on/off joins the morph field as a LEVEL RAMP — the lead's ruling was wrong and the human caught it** (human 2026-09-22: "Sub on/off is still exempt from morph and it ought to be wired in the way the other two oscs are (admittedly the oscillators have their own logic)"). **THE LEAD'S ERROR, stated plainly:** when engine blocks joined the field (B195) the lead kept the block's GATE out and was pleased with the code's justification — that 'the gate is not a corner value' is then a property of ONE rule rather than two lists. Internally tidy, and inconsistent with the instrument: **the oscillators' enable (id 150) IS in the field** and has been since 2026-08-26, handled by `morphApplyOscEnable` under B48's special case. The human's parenthesis — 'admittedly the oscillators have their own logic' — is exactly right and is the reason the ruling should have been theirs. **WHAT B48 ALREADY KNOWS, and the sub must inherit:** a stepped PICK drew enable from one corner while vol came from another, and the off transition hard-kills voices, so the boundary CLICKED and the partway state was a chimera. Instead the bilinear weight of the corners holding the osc ON becomes a GAIN RAMP through the existing ~8 ms smoother, and the stepped flip is deferred to the weight floor where the osc is already ~−60 dB — the kill and re-strike still run, inaudibly. Plain `w[]`, not the Gumbel draw and not the sharpened weights, so the ramp is deterministic in pad position under all three laws; at a pure corner the weight equals that corner's stored enable, so corners stay bit-identical. The sub has a level and a smoother, so the mechanism transfers. | B213 | **Units, tapers and tempo divisions — one plan before any code** (human 2026-09-22: "When a frequency parameter is set to Hz, it should show Hz; when it's set to tempo sync, it should be quantized to sensible divisions (and show the divisions). Timing parameters should be in ms or seconds, and their ranges should probably have a bit of a curve so you can control tiny changes and also reach big distances (this applies to envelopes, in particular). We can roadmap this process and plan it out before executing, just to make sure all bases are covered."). **PLAN FIRST; NOTHING IN THE PLUGIN CHANGES UNTIL THE HUMAN RULES ON THE DECISIONS BELOW.** **What the lead found in a first pass (2026-09-22), which is why this is a plan and not a patch:** a parameter's unit lives in THREE places that disagree — the C++ name string ('Bend Time (ms)'), the host's `params_value_to_text` (a hand-written id list: envelope times, glide, dissolve, octave and a few more; everything else, including every delay time and LFO rate, reaches the host as a bare `%.3f`), and `src/param_presentation.tsv`'s `unit` column (filled on 56 of 257 knobs; 25 more carry the unit only inside the label; 176 have none — corrected by the Phase 0 inventory, the row first said 201 by counting the label-only 25 twice). Tapers live only in the presentation table's `scale` column (log10 on 30 knobs) and so only in horde's own GUI: **the pitch envelope, ENV 3/4, the S.envelope and the sub's glide are all LINEAR seconds (the row first also named the mixer's crossfade, id 265 — it is buried and has no gui2 control, corrected by the inventory)**, which is exactly the envelope complaint. Tempo sync is a CONTINUOUS 0.0625–8 'beats' knob on the LFOs and delays (`lfoNBeats`, `dNbeats`), not a list of divisions; only the bend grid (param 23) names rational divisions today. **Phase 0 — inventory (read-only, dispatched now).** One table of every continuous parameter: address, range, default, current unit in each of the three places, current taper, host text today, sync partner if any, and a PROPOSED unit / taper / display format / range with a reason. Written to `docs/audits/`, not to code. **Phase 1 — the human's decisions:** (D1) **The taper law.** log10 (today) cannot reach zero, so an attack can never be 0 ms; a power/skew curve can, and bends less at the top. One law for all times, or log for frequencies and skew for times? (D2) **Host automation lanes.** CLAP parameters are linear in their own units, so in Ableton an attack's lane is linear 0.001–2 s and the tiny values are unreachable by drawing — the taper exists only in our GUI. Keep it (honest units, poor lanes), or expose a tapered 0..1 parameter (good lanes, but every existing set's automation and every preset's stored value would need conversion, on a frozen plugin id). This is an interface change and the biggest decision here. (D3) **Tempo divisions.** A named list (1/64 … 8 bars, with dotted and triplet) stored as a stepped index, or the continuous beats value kept and snapped on display and entry; and what an existing patch's in-between beat value becomes (snap to nearest, recorded). B208's lab proposes the list itself; this row adopts that proposal rather than writing a second one. (D4) **One ms/s rule everywhere** (e.g. under 1 s reads ms, 1 s and over reads s; Hz above 1 kHz reads kHz), applied identically in the GUI and the host text. (D5) **Ranges.** Envelope attack/decay/release reach, ENV 3/4 and the pitch envelope matched to the gain envelopes; widening a range keeps every stored value valid (values are stored in seconds), narrowing does not. (D6) **Morph and modulation in taper space.** Today a morph between 5 ms and 5 s interpolates linear seconds, so in BLEND mode it spends 60 % of the journey above 2 s; and a mod depth is a fraction of the LINEAR range, so it OVER-moves a short attack — depth 0.01 takes a 5 ms attack to 25 ms. (Both corrected by the inventory: the row first said 'almost the whole journey' and 'barely moves', the second in the wrong direction.) Should both work in the control's curved space instead? This changes how existing morphs and routes SOUND, so it is a ruling, not a fix. **Phase 2 — one source.** The presentation table's `unit` and `scale` become total for every continuous row (units out of the labels), and a check enforces it (a time row carries s/ms and a taper; a sync row carries a division list). **Phase 3 — derive, never copy.** The host's value-to-text and text-to-value are GENERATED from that table (the `gen_depends_header.py` pattern already exists), typed entry accepts '250 ms', '1.2 s', '2 kHz', '1/8T'; gui2's `fmtVal` formats with the same rule. **Phase 4 — the sync divisions and the curves**, as ruled in D1–D3 and D6. **Acceptance for the PLAN (this row's first deliverable):** the Phase 0 inventory landed, and D1–D6 each answered by the human and recorded in DECISIONS.md. Phases 2–4 get their own acceptance when ruled. **PHASE 0 LANDED 2026-09-22 → PR #728** (`docs/audits/2026-09-22-units-inventory.md`; lead re-ran verify fast on `324d50f`: exit 0; leak clean). All 266 continuous parameters, D1–D6 evidence, every rule hard-coded by id, and what could not be determined. Mostly OBSERVED: scratch probes loaded the plugin and read what a host reads, including a `text_to_value` round trip. Headlines: host text is osc-1-only (`id ==`, not `baseIdOf`, so osc 2's attack reaches the host as `0.003` while osc 1's reads `3.0 ms`); typed entry does not round-trip (`atof`, so the host's own `3.0 ms` comes back as 3 s); gui2's knob readout has no unit and no ms rule, so a 3 ms attack reads `0.00` — and 74 of the bank's 82 attack values are 6 ms or less; three rows declared log10 render LINEAR because the generator requires min > 0 (Glide, Morph Glide, Onset Scatter — D1 in miniature); ENV 2/3/4 and the S.envelope already share ENV 1's exact ranges and differ only in taper and text; the 'beats' parameters use two OPPOSITE conventions under one unit (LFO/delay beats are beats per cycle, the grids cycles per beat, all labelled `/beat`, and in the grid's naming '1/4' is a whole note); snapping to divisions changes NO factory patch or fixture; host lanes are linear and neither CLAP 1.2.10 nor clap-wrapper v0.15.1 has any taper hook (1–10 ms is the bottom 0.45 % of an attack lane); widening a range re-maps existing VST3/AU automation, because the wrapper normalises through min/max (from the wrapper code, not observed in a host); and 'Attack' means a one-pole time constant in five envelopes and a linear arrival time in the sub. **Answered by the lead from this session's record, which the inventory could not know:** the human's Ableton loads the VST3 — Ableton has no CLAP support — so D2 is decided on the VST3 path. **ORDERING, the inventory's best catch:** B208 proposes changing envelope times from time constants to arrival times, which changes every displayed attack by ×4.61 for the same sound. Rule B208's envelope-time law BEFORE D4, or every envelope number is relabelled twice. | § B128 · § B39 · § B208 · § ADR-009 · § ADR-169 |

Returned again. **REWORK 2 landed `c8580f2` — READY TO MERGE (APPROVE-WITH-NOTES, per the critic's stated condition, the lead having checked the final diff):** stepped slots compare exactly (row fails before, 999996/999999 → 999998/999998; passes after, with a unanimous-corners control that still adopts), and the quantum group rule's comment now gives its real reason (ADR-176 §3: under quantum you hear ONE corner's whole table) rather than a cycle hazard that cannot occur today. (implementer's verify full exit 0 on `c868e73`, 0 FAIL lines; leak clean). Each cause shown by a failing row, a must-read-zero control and a planted failure; reverting each fix alone re-reddens its own rows. (1) **Morph on DID make a node** — the END mark overwrote its label with the display name 'Morph', and the panel merges consecutive same-label nodes, so on-then-off showed as 'Morph ×2'. Fix: the pending 'morph on'/'morph off' label is kept. (3) **Snapshots already restored byte-identically — which is why the B186 gauntlet stayed green — but routing was in NO snapshot (B193, a cause, folded in) and a morph-on node rewrites routing from its corners as soon as audio runs; with that fixed, a second cause surfaced: history rounded corner values to 6 significant digits.** Fix: history nodes store `historyJson` = the preset JSON plus an always-present `routing` key, corners and mod-route depths at full precision. **Presets and the host chunk are claimed untouched** — B193's literal fix (routing in `stateJson`) was REFUSED as a preset-format change, correctly. (pinned as a boundary row that goes red when decided); (b) HOST AUTOMATION of morph on after a load still reverts live edits, kept so existing sessions play back unchanged — confirm; (c) in-flight motion (morph glide `morphCur`, master-volume declick `masterVolSm`) is not restored — a node recorded mid-glide returns at its target (≤ 0.063 peak under a long Morph Glide); snapping either would change existing renders. | B232 | **Blend ignores a corner where the source is OFF — the human's rule, not yet the code's** (human 2026-09-23: "if one morph corner has, say, Osc 2 turned off and the other has it on, instead of blending from corner 1's irrelevant Osc 2 settings, the blend effectively treats corner 1 as if it has corner 2's osc 2 with the level at 0 … this is also how the Sub should work when blend is on"). **What the code does TODAY (read by the lead, `src/hypersaw_clap.cpp` morphStep ~4200-4245):** the on/off itself is B48/B203's LEVEL RAMP (the gain is the bilinear share of corners holding the source ON, the hard flip deferred to ~−60 dB) — that part matches the human's picture. Declared by GATE, not by the depends graph — each engine row maps to its block's `gateId`, each osc row to `150 + k·1000`, the ids the level ramp already reads — for four reasons: depends would hide an off source's panel, the SUB's dependencies live in `shown_when`, the generator flattens AND to OR, and a depends declaration would ALSO change ADR-108's quantum-path hold, which is not revision-gated. Floor 1e-3 (the ramp's own threshold, now `kMorphOnFloor`); stepped, quantum pick, exempt and the intent-bus path (owner-picks, no blend) unchanged; `morphRouteEdit` uses the same weights (else a live edit at the midpoint lands 0.85 and is overwritten next tick); an all-corners-agree fallback avoids a one-ulp drift. `offcorner_check` (new, WIRED into full): 14 failures on main, 0 after; revision-1 render hashes identical to main; **all 41 factory patches at 11 pad positions each, 451 of 451 renders bit-identical between revisions** — no factory patch has a source off in only some corners, so the bank moved to revision 2 without re-voicing anything. One remaining path to S1: switching a GATE on directly (GUI click or host automation) while morph is on still glides from the OFF corner, because the enable is committed before the morph tick reads it (detune 0.31 → 0.147 over 500 ms toward the OFF corner's 0.1, audible throughout). | B235 | **Custom blend curves on the morph pad** (human 2026-09-23: "in the same way that we'll be able to edit the quantum boundaries on the quantum morph, would it make sense to be able to add custom curves to blend parameters? … you move the morph point to a position and then go down to the parameter list and set the parameter to where you want it at that point and the curves are calculated from there. Design standard as the 2026-09-22 batch: gui2's `:root` tokens, `docs/design-system/` (ADR-116), `docs/design/station-page-lab.html` as the model; both themes; loads under `lab_load_check`; `lab-review` meta updated. **BUILT 2026-09-24 → PR #742** (verify fast exit 0 on `09c1f8c`; leak clean). Every draw is the ENGINE'S OWN LFO stream (patch seed XOR 0x9E3779B9, 2u−1), read by cycle number so picture and sound call one function; a C++ program on the engine's `rngNext` prints the same first 8 draws to 12 decimals. | B229 | **Envelope architecture redesign — the Serum 2 model** (human 2026-09-23: "I'm starting to think we need to redesign the envelope system; Serum 2 provides a good model, where Env 1 is a global level envelope but levels can be individually modulated with other envelopes and LFOs, etc. This is a cleaner system than the one we've started with here, though I know it will break older patches if we don't start versioning the plugin or something."). **The versioning already exists (B100):** every blob carries `engine_revision`, and a sound-changing law lands behind a revision gate, so a patch saved under revision 1 keeps rendering with revision-1 laws until the patch itself is opted forward (`src/hypersaw_clap.cpp` 'B100 STATE HEADER'). So: ENV 1 is a GLOBAL pre-FX amplitude envelope bounding every oscillator (both swarms AND the sub — which is how the sub gets its missing decay/sustain) and the pre-FX filter outputs; per-oscillator and per-filter LEVELS become ordinary destinations other modulators shape within that bound; revision-gated (ADR-183 path). Let's do a pared down lab prototype for it."), after the human's objection that per-patch structure would make oscillator and FX presets unloadable. The model as accepted: (1) **VALUES are per corner** — everything that is a parameter (swarm/sub/SCALPEL settings incl. modes and on/off, modulator settings, route DEPTHS, FX module parameters); an oscillator preset writes into one corner or all four, never a conflict. (2) **SHARED LISTS are per patch and only GROW** — which routes exist and which modulators are in use; a preset ADDS to them, a route a corner does not use sits at depth 0 there; the only conflict is a full list, and the load says so. (3) **RACK LINEUP is per SIDE** — at most two racks, A on the left (corners A, C) and B on the right (B, D); X crossfades their audio, each corner sets its side's parameters; an FX preset loads into a side and is the one true structural swap. (4) **MOD-BANK ZONES** — the global bank is fixed-size with a zone per part (source, rack A, rack B, global), so a part's modulators land in its own zone and never collide. Acceptance: presets of each kind load as the table says (osc → a corner or all; rack → a side; routes add at depth 0 elsewhere; a full list refuses with a message); the two racks crossfade on X with a stated fixed cost; zones never collide; a lock holds under morph; a self-check with must-fail controls; both themes; loads under lab_load_check. | § B258 · § B257 · § B72 · § ADR-109 · § B170 |

| B265 | **The FX-chain morph algorithm — pared to its core, raced in a lab** (human 2026-09-25: "I still want there to be a stochastic or, when achievable, gradual flow from left to right. There need to be different orders in which the FX can be arranged … a bounded domain based on common and tested experimental configurations … 4. When modules are arranged differently, there needs to be some logic for swapping parameters with other instances of the same module, switching the order of modules, shuffling together modules in a rational order. Let's pare this challenge down to the simplest format that preserves the mathematical dynamics of the problem and then work through alternatives in a lab."). **The pared problem (the lead's formulation):** 4 module types (Drive, Filter, Delay, Reverb), at most ONE of each, so a chain is an ORDERED SUBSET and cost is bounded by construction (≤ 4 live modules at any x); 2 input lanes (Body, Sub); two endpoint patches L and R, each with an order, lane→module routing, per-module parameters and optionally one feedback edge; a morph position x plus a seed and a temperature. Parameter matching is BY TYPE (one per type makes it unambiguous). **Invariants at every x:** (I1) one per type; (I2) acyclic except at most one feedback edge with bounded gain; (I3) NO EDGE MID-MORPH THAT EXISTS AT NEITHER END — the 'sub feeding the reverb' failure as a checkable rule; (I4, optional) every intermediate order is from an approved set; (I5) every structural event is crossfaded and events are spread across x by seeded thresholds, never stacked at one point. (I6, added by the human 2026-09-25: "there needs to be a way to enforce that every input reaches an output; I don't want any intermediate morph states where all paths from an osc to an output are severed") EVERY INPUT LANE REACHES THE OUTPUT AT EVERY x — stated on GAIN, not topology: each lane's total transmission to the output stays ≥ a stated floor across the sweep, which catches break-before-make crossfades (an old edge fading out before its replacement fades in) as well as a lane whose only path runs through a module being removed; the remedy is make-before-break, and the must-fail plant is the same morph with the crossfade order reversed. (I7, added by the human 2026-09-25: "no node (aside from sound-generating nodes) without any inputs should have outputs") A PROCESSING NODE WITH NO INPUT MUST NOT OUTPUT — on the gain graph, a module's output edges may be live only while its input transmission is above a floor; for wiring changes, inputs connect before outputs and outputs disconnect before inputs (the dual of I6's make-before-break). Open reading: a delay or reverb whose input fades still rings — STRICT (its output must fade with its input) or TAIL-ALLOWED (it may ring out); the test measures both. **Alternatives to race:** (A) rank-key interpolation — interpolate each module's position between L and R, order = sort, seed breaks ties; (B) edit path — the minimal sequence of adjacent swaps, inserts and removals, each at a seeded threshold; (C) approved-order graph — a curated set of tested orders linked by single swaps, morph walks a path through it; (D) naive slot splicing — the CONTROL, expected to violate I1 and I3. Routing: edge weights crossfade; I3 pins never-present edges at zero. Feedback: none vs one bounded return edge with placement rules. **Metrics per algorithm:** invariants held (with must-fail plants), structural events across x, worst audible jump in a render, and DISTINCT intermediate chains (exploration as a number). **Acceptance:** the four algorithms running side by side on shared endpoint pairs (including an adversarial pair designed to tempt I3), the metrics table, audible, both themes, loads under lab_load_check, pinned in the navigator. **LAB BUILT 2026-09-25 → PR #755** (verify fast exit 0 on `aebf6de`; leak clean; self-check 12/12 claims with 12/12 planted faults caught; navigator regenerated in the PR). **The central finding: the invariants are not a property of the ORDER algorithm.** A, B and C only choose which orders the chain passes through; ONE shared ROUTER under all three holds I1, I2, I3 and I6 — input ports whose old sources fade out as new ones fade in, per-edge seeded crossfades, an edge allowed only while it runs forward in the current order, make-before-break for I6, and a reach guard. The click fell from 10–12 dB as the human heard it to 4.4 dB; the worst reversal is 5.9 dB. Claim 9 sets a ≤ 7 dB ceiling. **Sluice's lessons, measured:** equal-gain p = 1 cut the worst step click 4.3 → 1.7 dB (now the lab default; a product default needs an ADR and a migration); the feedback delay is now one sample, with renders bit-identical across buffers 64/128/512 while a loop is live (claim 11; CPU 39 vs 25 ms/s while looping); the loop limiter is an off-by-default dev toggle (−36 dB effect, no click change); woken modules jump to their targets (the ECHO was 33 ms off; claim 10), which exposed and fixed a latent ECHO NaN. **Gain staging:** the hottest point inside the chain fell +4.1 → −0.4 dBFS; output peak −6.4 dBTP worst; no clipping; no limiter. **Layouts:** RING, RACK, MATRIX, FLOW, PANEL (Eurorack), ROLL (history), behind a selector that persists the choice. **Layout ruling 2026-10-08**, human verbatim: "I like the rack, the matrix, and the panel (I think each could be designed a little more elegantly, but the general concepts are good). I think each should be visible." **Round 3c BUILT (lab PR #985, stacked on #982; verify fast and full 0; self-check 12/12 claims and faults).** RACK, MATRIX and PANEL are shown together from one cable state; RING, FLOW and ROLL are removed; each view is a pure scene builder with a thin painter. There is one visual language: a colour per module (a departure from ADR-116 colour roles, flagged in code), thickness and opacity for weight, dashed z⁻¹ for backward cables, amber halo for loops, amber dots for waits, ✕ for prohibited. Claim 12: across 26,600 states every view draws exactly the engine's live cables, bit for bit. Open for the human: whether the per-module palette reads (and whether gui3 should adopt it); PANEL density; whether views glide without audio. |

(1) A PROPERTY-BASED FUZZER over B265's world (four types, one each; Body and Sub lanes): thousands of seeded random endpoint pairs plus the adversarial ones, across temperatures and seeds, every paradigm checked against I1–I7 (I7 both readings) — the failure rate per invariant per paradigm, and every failure SHRUNK to its minimal counterexample so the design sees cases, not percentages. (2) THE PARADIGMS: the lab's A (rank keys), B (edit path), C (approved-order graph), D (slot splice, control) with the shared router, PLUS four architectures that avoid order collisions BY CONSTRUCTION: E fixed canonical order with a per-module mix (order never morphs; 'absent' = mix 0; order variety chosen per patch from a small set); F per-module series↔parallel blend; G lanes with a forward-only send matrix (acyclic by construction; order = which lane feeds which); H continuous positions on one spine. One pure model shared by the lab and the fuzzer; I7 on the gain graph in two readings (STRICT: a live output needs input ≥ 0.5 absolute; TAIL: a Delay/Reverb may ring for 0.1 of x without rising); a WIRING PLANNER that searches single edge changes through states that each hold I2, I3·path, I6 and I7 — an exhausted search is a PROOF no legal sequence exists. **Fuzz, 2000 pairs × 4 temperatures × 2 seeds = 16 000 runs per paradigm:** A, B, C (the order algorithms on the shared router) break I7 in 46–51 % of runs — the minimal counterexample is ONE module (dry → a Reverb): the router gives each port its own seeded time, so a module's input and output fade in together, and no order algorithm can fix a router-timing fault; D breaks everything. The collision-free architectures on the planner — E (fixed order + mix), F (series↔parallel), G (lanes + forward sends), H (continuous positions), and the hybrid GC (G walking C's approved graph) — hold EVERY claimed invariant in every hosted run (0 broken claims, asserted by the gate). Gap: 0.2 % of runs are provably impossible under the approved set (e.g. Rv Dl Dr is missing) — add the order or fall back to F. **Open, for the human:** I7 means 'has input', absolute (the agent's first relative floor produced false failures); STRICT or TAIL; add Rv Dl Dr to the approved set or allow F's jump; temperature 0 packs moves one crossfade apart around x = 0.5 (the fastest legal cut) rather than B265's single hard cut; E's I3 edge-reading failures vanish under the path reading. `verify full` grows by ~29 s. | § B265 · § B263 · § B50 |

| B253 | **Coherence (R) as a modulation source** (human 2026-09-24: "R needs to be a modulation source; please make sure it's in the Mod lab if it isn't already."). It is not: the shipped matrix carries 22 sources and none is R; slots 22 and 23 of `kMaxSources` are free. (1) The mod matrix lab (`docs/design/mod-matrix-lab.html`) gains Coherence 1 and Coherence 2 at slots 22/23, driven by a real Kuramoto order parameter in the lab (not a stand-in curve), unipolar 0..1, with its natural motion shown (it rises as the swarm locks and falls under negative coupling). (2) The questions the engine port must answer, which the lab should make concrete: R is PER NOTE (each voice's swarm has its own) — so a global source needs a rule (the loudest voice's, the mean, the newest note's), or R is a per-voice source; and routing R back into Coupling is a feedback loop that the one-tick delay makes stable but not necessarily tame. **BUILT (lab) 2026-09-24 → PR #747** (verify fast exit 0 on `bd637ab`; leak clean). Coherence 1/2 at slots 22/23, unipolar, driven by a seeded per-note Kuramoto swarm that follows `src/swarm_core.h`'s law line by line (cited); a three-note chord shows each note's own R; self-check K +1 × 7 members 0.965, K −1 × 4 members 0.046, two planted wrong laws refused. **Behaviour:** a strike starts at R = 1 (phases restart), then locks above K ≈ 0.75 at every detune (the coupling is scaled by the pitch spread), wanders below, falls toward 0 under negative K. **Recommendation:** a PER-VOICE source wherever the destination can be per note; GAIN-WEIGHTED where it must be global (largest one-tick step 0.32, against 0.90 for newest, 0.73 for max). **Feedback into Coupling is stable by construction** and indifferent to the one-tick delay; the SIGN decides: +0.5 LATCHES at R 0.97 and re-striking cannot free it, +0.25 BURSTS (catch, hold, release — the musically interesting one), −0.5 GOVERNS (never locks). **Consequence:** with Coherence at 22/23 the source table (`kMaxSources` 24) is FULL — B180's per-osc Gain ENVs and SCALPEL's new sources both need the cap to grow (relayed to B252's accounting). Open: does voice gain include velocity (the lab weights velocity × envelope); should a latched loop be flagged in the UI; the coherence self-check lives only in the page, not in `./verify`. | § B207 · § B179 · § ADR-136 |
