A lab that invents its own palette is not current, however good it looks. **What exists and what does not:** a corner today is CAPTURED whole — you set the instrument, then store it into a corner — and there is no way to see or edit a corner's values parameter by parameter. The field has grown this week: engine blocks joined it (B195), the sub's gate joined as a ramp (B203), and membership has three categories that behave differently (continuous rows interpolate, structural rows snap atomically, the gates ramp). An expanded editor has to show which is which, or a player will not understand why one value slides and its neighbour jumps. **Questions the lab should make answerable:** a table or a grid of four corners × every morphable parameter, and how to make that navigable at ~270 rows; editing one corner's value directly without disturbing the live sound; showing EXEMPT parameters (ADR-109) distinctly from absent ones; and showing where the pad currently sits so a value can be read as 'what this corner holds' versus 'what you are hearing now'. The intent bus (B170) is deliberately out of scope — it re-shapes the field and the editor should not wait for it. ACCEPTANCE: to standard, loading and screenshotted in both themes; per-corner per-parameter editing prototyped against a realistic field (real parameter names and classes, not placeholders); the three membership behaviours visually distinct; exempt shown distinctly from absent. **BUILT 2026-09-22 → PR #724.** New file `docs/design/morph-editor-lab.html` (the named starting point `quantum-morph-lab.html` is gitignored and local-only, so the agent ported `src/morph_core.h` instead). The REAL field, dumped from the plugin's own debug and CLAP info at 3fd3a6b: **273 members — 181 continuous, 89 structural, 3 gates** (osc enables 150/1150, the sub's 4015), shown against the four corners of the factory patch 'MO - Quantum Morph'. Default view is only the rows whose corners DIFFER (15 of 273), with section jumps, gui2's groups, and a search that also finds non-members. Each kind has a glyph, a word and its own cell form (SLIDES bar / SNAPS pill / RAMPS switch), and the pad paints the selected row across every position. A cell edit is STAGED and says before commit what it would change at the current pad position. Exempt is a ⊘ band with a value and a way back; the 124 non-members have no cells, only the shell's reason, in their own section. Self-check against the engine's `morphOwnersJson`: 1092/1092 (4 pad positions × 273), with must-fail controls at 1091 and 634. Not measured: blended values and gate ramp levels are a port, not compared. **Open, for the human:** STAGING needs only a GUI buffer, but today the shell's armed-corner edit is heard at the next grid tick whenever that corner contributes — staged or live? The field table is a SNAPSHOT and a port must read it from the shell. | § B195 · § B203 · § ADR-109 · § ADR-159 |
| B206 | **A never-activated instance saves without its engine blocks** (found by B204's activation control, 2026-09-22, and the control is why it was not reported as a defect in the round trip). A chunk round trip APPEARS to lose the whole SUB block, and is byte-identical once the instance is activated — so the agent's first reading (a state defect) was wrong and its own control caught it. What remains is narrow but real: `state_save` on an instance that has been created but never activated omits the engine block, so a host that saved at that moment would write a patch with no sub. Hosts do create-without-activate during scanning, and a scan does not normally save, which is why this is a row and not an alarm. Decide whether the block should be present from construction (the gate ships OFF, so emitting it costs nothing and removes a state that depends on lifecycle) or whether save-before-activate is a contract violation worth asserting against instead. | § B172 · § B204 |
| B205 | **The sub's mono re-strike still clicks when VELOCITY changes — measured, ungated, and the fix was refused for a good reason** (found by B202's own rig, 2026-09-22). With the phase preserved, a re-strike at constant velocity is clean (1.44× the natural step) but a re-strike from velocity 1.0 to 0.3 still steps **11.91×**, because the level jumps under a live tail even though the phase no longer does. Reported and printed, deliberately NOT gated. **The fix the agent identified and then declined:** give mono's re-strike a FREE SLOT, which is what the swarm's own mono already does for a ringing tail ('a fresh strike on a new slot, overlapping the tail naturally'). It was refused as outside an implementer's remit, correctly — it rewrites B181's documented contract that the sub has ONE SOUNDING SLOT AND IT IS SLOT 0, and it silently changes what `subWaveJson`'s instance-0 `freqHz()` means, which is the frequency the wave display prints in its header. That is an interface and architecture change wearing a bug fix's clothes. Queue it with a critic, not an implementer. The question to settle first: does the sub become polyphonic-with-one-audible-voice (the swarm's shape, which makes the overlap free) or does it keep one slot and cross-fade the level (cheaper, and it keeps the display honest)? | § B202 · § B181 · § ADR-099 |
| B204 | **Saving a set with horde in it got slower — two candidates measured and RULED OUT, one identified, the measurement not yet taken** (human 2026-09-22: "Also noticing it's taking longer to save sets with Horde in them. We may want to look into this"). **RULED OUT BY MEASUREMENT, not by argument.** (i) STATE SIZE: the chunk is **9.5 KB** and grew **84 bytes** across this week's work (9381 → 9465 bytes on the same factory patch, measured at three commits) — twenty sub ids, twenty modulator ids, the preset name and eight more entries per corner cost almost nothing, and 9 KB cannot be a perceptible save. (ii) DISK I/O IN THE SAVE PATH: `state_save` builds a key=value string and touches no file; the GUI's preset JSON is CACHED per name (`presetJsonCache`), so the asterisk does not re-read from disk on each poll. **THE REMAINING CANDIDATE, and why it is plausible without being proven:** the GUI's 500 ms poll now marshals the whole preset JSON across the webview bridge for the global dirty test (`hzPresetDirty`, ~9.5 KB) PLUS the four corner dirty tests (`hzMorphCornerDirty`, ~700 bytes each), and each is a full parse and compare in the shell — roughly 12 KB and five comparisons twice a second, where before B174 there were four. That is a CONTINUOUS cost rather than a save-time one, but a host's save waits on the plugin's main thread, so a busy main thread can show up exactly as the human describes. **Not asserted — measured next.** The measurement wants: `state_save`'s own wall time through the CLAP factory, the poll's cost per tick, and the same with the dirty tests disabled as the control. If it IS the poll, the fix is cheap and obvious in hindsight: compare a HASH rather than the document, or only re-test when a parameter actually changed (the GUI already knows, since it marks history on every edit). **ESCALATED 2026-09-22: the human had to FORCE QUIT — this is a HANG with unsaved work at risk, not a slow path.** Ableton's log shows horde loaded over VST3 and ends after two save attempts (21:40:56, 21:45:22) with no clean shutdown and no macOS hang report. Further ruled out by reading: `state_save`'s write loop bails correctly on a non-positive return (not an infinite loop); there is no `std::mutex`, `lock_guard`, `dispatch_sync` or `performSelectorOnMainThread` anywhere in the shell or the GUI layer, so no classic deadlock in our code; and `libs/clap-wrapper` is pinned at the commit tagged v0.15.1 matching CLAUDE.md (`git describe` reports `v0.7.1-144-g35f524b`, which is misleading and NOT a version mismatch). **CORRECTION FROM THE HUMAN, 2026-09-22: "Ableton doesn't natively support CLAP."** The lead had framed VST3 as a choice they made. It is not — VST3 is the only path Ableton offers, so **the wrapper layer is in EVERY save they will ever do**, and 'does it stall on CLAP' is not a test available in their host. The narrowing test is therefore the **AU**: it is a DIFFERENT wrapper shim in the SAME host, we ship and install it, and their log shows it created successfully on 2026-09-20. If VST3 stalls and AU does not, the fault is the VST3 shim specifically; if both stall, it is our plugin or the wrapper core. That test costs the human one plugin swap and no build. **MEASURED 2026-09-22 → PR #719, AND THE LEAD'S HYPOTHESIS IS REFUTED.** Two diagnostics built: `tools/save_bench.cpp` (CLAP factory) and `tools/vst3_save_bench.cpp`, which loads the BUILT `horde.vst3` the way a host does (CFBundle → `bundleEntry` → `GetPluginFactory` → `createInstance` → `setupProcessing` → `setActive`) and times `IComponent::getState` — so the VST3 number is measured on the path the human actually uses, not substituted from the CLAP one. **`state_save` is 105.50 µs default / 240.92 µs adversarial on CLAP, and 172.33 / 213.17 µs through VST3.** Microseconds. **B174's `hzPresetDirty` is ~1.0 ms and B122's four corner tests are 15 µs, against a 198 µs control with both removed — a marginal 1.1 ms twice a second, 0.22 % of one core.** The poll cannot stall a host, and the lead's suspicion of it was wrong. Nothing in the save path grows with session length either: the undo ring is fixed at 200, is never in the chunk, and `state_save` measures 135.54 µs on an empty history against 135.17 µs on a full one. **THE MEASUREMENT INVERTS THE TEST, which is its most useful product.** The prediction is now that **closing the window makes NO difference**. If it DOES make the stall disappear, the cause is main-thread contention that is not this 1.1 ms, and the next place to look is the host's servicing of the webview itself rather than anything our poll computes. The AU remains the second discriminator (a different shim, same host). **B204 STAYS OPEN WITH NO IDENTIFIED CAUSE.** Everything above refutes candidates; none of it diagnoses the hang, and the agent could not reproduce it. That is the correct outcome for a measurement brief and it is also the honest state of the row. Two findings kept for later rather than folded away: `presetMatches`' millisecond is 1026 µs of 1089 in per-key needle construction and `find` (only 6.6 µs is `atof` over 368 keys, and a document 27× longer only doubles the time), so hoisting the 368 needles is the cheap half IF a fix is ever wanted for other reasons; and `syncPresetName`/`syncCornerNames` carry NO in-flight guard where `frameFetch` has `frameBusy` — at 1.1 ms against a 500 ms tick that is a shape rather than a cause, but it is the shape that makes a stall WORSE once one begins, because the polls keep queuing work while the thread is blocked. | § B174 · § B122 · § B41 · § ADR-002 |
| B201 | **A morph that relocates Comb drops it, for the same reason a load used to** (found by B188's fix, 2026-09-22). Morph writes slot types at the same choke point as a load but with `loadingState` false, so it takes the LIVE path where the singleton cap refuses the arriving Comb against a still-fading shadow. B188 fixed the load path deliberately narrowly — ending a blocking fade only for load-path writes — because widening it unconditionally turned `fxxfade_check` T4 red, and that red is the correct boundary for a LIVE edit: a player adding a second Comb while the first fades should still be refused. A morph is neither: it is not a player's edit and not a whole-patch load, it is the field moving between authored states, and nobody has said which path it should take. **That is the ruling this row wants**, and it is the same question B117's crossfade poses generally — whether a morph's slot change is a handover (fade, like an edit) or a restoration (immediate, like a load). Gated by nothing today. | § B188 · § B117 · § B186 |
| B200 | **`./verify fast` can be green on a tree that does not compile** (found BY the B190 work producing it, 2026-09-21). A prose edit deleted a closing `*/` from a check file; `fast` reported green because **`fast` builds nothing** — it is the paperwork leg by design (1.5 s: declarations, coverage, the leak gate) and `full` is where the compiler runs. That division is deliberate and mostly right, but it has a sharp edge: `fast` is what CI blocks on for a docs-only change, what the session-end hook runs, and therefore what a session can close green on while the tree is broken. The agent that hit it said so rather than quietly fixing the symptom, which is how it reached this row. OPTIONS, with their cost against the measured 1.5 s: (a) add `-fsyntax-only` over the tools and headers — catches exactly this class, and the cost is the question (estimate it before choosing, since `fast` runs at every session end and its whole value is being cheap enough to run constantly); (b) leave `fast` alone and accept that a broken tree is caught by `full` and by CI's build legs — true today, and it means the session-end gate cannot make that promise; (c) have the Stop hook run something that compiles, moving the cost off CI and onto the boundary where the damage is done. **Lead leans (a) IF the measurement is small** — a syntax pass is not a build and the files are small — and (b) if it is not, with the limitation then written into `fast`'s own header so nobody reads its green as more than it means. The human rules once the number exists. | § ADR-180 · § B190 · § B159 |
| B199 | **Per-parameter safe modulation rates — measure the artifact, derive the smoothing, and let the classes decide who is in the table** (human 2026-09-21: "different parameters probably have different safe modulation rate limits. We should probably run a test on all of them and create a table logging when each one breaks so we can determine a system for ideal behavior beyond those points. Let me know if this is an XY problem though"). **Lead's answer: not an XY problem — the measurement is real and nothing in the repo has it — but "when it breaks" conflates FIVE failure modes with five different fixes, and a single table of breaking points would flatten them.** They are: (1) DISCONTINUITY — no smoothing, so a step clicks; measurable as step size against the signal's own natural slope, and the repo already measures exactly this (STATION's rows: matrix cells 1.10× natural, op LVL 2.33× before smoothing landed). (2) STRUCTURALLY UNINTERPOLATABLE — waveform, mode, algorithm: no smoothing helps because fast modulation IS switching; already declared by `paramClassOf` and already snapped atomically in the morph field, so these are excluded from the table BY CLASS rather than by measurement. (3) STABILITY — filter cutoff and resonance, feedback amounts: fast coefficient movement can destabilise a filter that is stable at every static setting, which is a different question from whether it clicks. (4) COST — a write that runs an expensive recompute: the sub's `recalc()` is 282 transcendentals and `bumpAmt`/`bumpPhase` are morphable, so the matrix can drive it per block; that is a CPU cliff, not an audio artifact, and it belongs on its own axis. (5) THE MODULATION RATE ITSELF — the mod tick is `kGravGridSeconds` ≈ 172 Hz, so modulation above ~86 Hz aliases in the modulator regardless of destination; that is a global ceiling, not a per-parameter fact, and B171 recorded the square/S&H case as arithmetic rather than a measured defect. **REFRAMED DELIVERABLE:** for every CONTINUOUS destination, sweep modulation rate and depth and measure the artifact against a stated threshold, then publish the DERIVED quantity — the smoothing time constant each destination needs — rather than a breaking point, because a breaking point is threshold-dependent while a time constant is actionable and can be asserted. The table's value is then finding the EXCEPTIONS: most destinations will want the same smoothing and the interesting output is the handful that do not, plus any that cannot be smoothed and must be crossfaded. Shape it like the SAW fidelity suite (measured thresholds, a stated margin, a must-fail control per row) and wire it; `paramClassOf` supplies membership so a new parameter is covered without anyone remembering, which is the property B191's gate just proved worth having. Sequencing: cheap to start and independent of the GUI batch; it wants the mod matrix stable, which it is. Open for the human when the numbers exist: whether an over-rate modulation should be CLAMPED (safe, silently different from what the patch asked for), SMOOTHED HARDER (safe, audibly laggy), or LEFT (honest, occasionally ugly) — that is a taste ruling the measurements should inform rather than pre-empt. | § B171 · § ADR-009 · § ADR-173 · § B41 |
| B198 | **Does "a load is a load" extend to RNG stream IDENTITY? — a ruling nobody has made** (surfaced by B192, 2026-09-21). The `ens=` and `lfo=` chunk fields are stream CONTINUATIONS, not patch values: `initState` deliberately does not reset them and the site says so (L0036). So a load restores every parameter but leaves the noise and ensemble streams where they were — which means two loads of the same patch are byte-identical in state and NOT identical in what they render next. That is defensible (a stream is session identity, like a voice's phase) and it is also the one hole in B192's byte-identity guarantee, which holds only on a corpus where neither stream had drawn. Nobody has ruled it, no row asked it, and the answer changes what "reproducible" means for a patch: reset on load makes a patch a complete description of a sound, while carrying on makes it a description of a sound *plus where the session had got to*. The lead leans CARRY ON, matching the comment's existing reasoning, and notes that the alternative would make every preset load re-draw the ensemble timing the human tuned. **RULED 2026-09-21 (human): "I suspect the ensemble random issue will be so minute that it will basically never become an issue. Let's keep as-is for now."** The streams carry on across a load; `initState` continues not to reset them. The consequence stated once so nobody re-derives it: B192's byte-identity guarantee is about STATE and not about the next sample rendered — two loads of one patch agree on every stored value and may differ in where the ensemble and noise streams had got to. "For now" is doing work: if a bounce ever fails to reproduce, this row is the first place to look, and the falsifier is a rendered A/B that a human can hear. | § B192 · § L0036 · § ADR-077 |
| B196 | **The Sub Osc joins the bend-law section on MAIN and loses its own glide; it defaults to "follow bend"** (human 2026-09-21: "Sub Osc should have its own region on the bend law section on main instead of its own glide within its module. It should default to 'follow bend' like the others"). This RETIRES part of B181 note 2, which the human asked for four days ago and has now seen in use: the sub got `sub.glide` as a knob inside its own panel, and the instrument already has a LANE-BASED bend architecture on MAIN — note pitch, bend wheel, mod wheel and MPE per-note bend each with their own law (ids 106-115 bend, 137-149 note travel), the whole point of which is that a lane's travel is described once and shared. A module carrying a private glide knob is the second copy of an idea the instrument already owns, and the human is right that it belongs in the lane section. Build: the sub becomes a LANE in the bend-law section with its own region, defaulting to **follow bend** (the same default the other lanes carry, so the sub tracks the instrument unless told otherwise); `sub.glide` (4018) is RETIRED IN PLACE — the block's id map is positional (`id − 4000` IS `SubOscCore::Param` for the core rows, and the shell block continues past it), so deleting it would move the ids after it, exactly as B184 established when hard sync left. Same treatment: the id stays reserved and marked, a retirement pin asserts writing it changes nothing, and the control disappears from the panel. Open question for the build, not for the human: whether "follow bend" means the sub shares the bend lane's law object or holds its own instance defaulted to match — the first is one law and cannot drift, the second lets a player give the sub a different feel later. Lead leans SHARE with a per-lane override added only when asked, on the reduce-never-invent rule. | § B181 · § ADR-112 · § B184 |
| B197 | **A lightweight drive for the Sub Osc — mild amp-style saturation, few controls, and possibly a high-end crunch; workshop it in a lab first** (human 2026-09-21: "Sub Osc should also have its own lightweight drive module, some kind of saturator with mild amp-style distortion (a small number of controls). And possibly a way to add a little high-end noise crunch like Ableton's erosion. We can workshop this with a lab to get it right"). **The human named the method and it is the repo's own:** a LAB first, then a port with the lab as the parity oracle (ADR-003). Every engine here arrived that way and the two that did not — the ones audited in September — are where the expedients were found. Scope discipline this row exists to hold: **small.** The instrument already has MAW as FX-C (ADR-092 amendment, ADR-170) — a Roar-class three-stage saturator with fourteen curves, an ecology stage and a feedback route — and the temptation will be to reach for it or to grow this into a second one. This is deliberately NOT that: it is a per-source colouring stage on the sub's own row, a handful of controls, sized so a bass patch gets weight and grit without visiting the rack. If the lab starts growing curve tables, that is the signal it has become MAW and should stop. The erosion idea is a SEPARATE mechanism from saturation and should be evaluated as one: a band-limited noise crunch (the reference is Ableton's Erosion — a narrow noise-modulated band, not broadband hiss) is a different animal from a transfer curve and may or may not earn its place beside it; the lab is where that is decided by ear, not by argument. Sequencing: after the current state-correctness batch (B195/B192) so the sub's parameter block is stable before it grows; the lab itself is cheap and can start any time the human wants to hear something. Open for the human when the lab exists: whether this lives on the sub ALONE or becomes a per-source stage every row gets (the swarm oscillators would want it too), which is a bigger question and the reason to build the lab before the id block. | § ADR-003 · § ADR-092 · § ADR-170 · § B172 |
| B194 | **Id 1043 is declared and reaches nothing** (found by B191's layer 4, 2026-09-21). It is the osc-2 twin of base 43, which is patch-scope, so writing 1043 leaves the snapshot unchanged — the only non-routing parameter in the table for which that is true. A parameter-table question rather than a history one: either the twin should not exist, or base 43's scope is mis-declared. Small, and it is the kind of thing that only surfaces when something enumerates the WHOLE table and asks what each entry does. | § B191 · § ADR-173 |
| B192 | **A factory Init patch, and initialise BEFORE every load** (human 2026-09-21: "when I turn on the Sub and then load a preset, the sub is still on in all of them. Maybe this is a more general issue of the patch not initializing before loading. Let's make sure there's a factory Init patch and that everything initializes as the first step before a load"). **FIRST, THE PART THAT IS ALREADY FIXED AND WAS NOT INSTALLED:** B181 note 6 changed `applyStateJson` so a parameter ABSENT from a loaded patch restores its DEFAULT rather than keeping whatever it held — which is precisely the sub-stays-on symptom. The human's installed build was `eb02e4b` (PR #696), and B181 landed in #699 AFTER it, so they were testing the pre-fix binary. Reinstalled 2026-09-21. The observation was right; the diagnosis of a general initialisation gap is ALSO right, and stands on its own. **WHY THE STRONGER GUARANTEE IS WORTH BUILDING ANYWAY:** "every loop defaults its absent keys" is three loops (the instrument table, the engine blocks, the osc-2 twins) that must EACH be right forever, and B183 already records that `state_load` — the DAW-session restore path — still carries the old skip. "Reset to init, then apply the patch" is ONE rule, checkable in one place, and it covers what a key-by-key default cannot: modulation routes, the intent chunk, corner state, engine blocks, and whatever the next module adds. Build: an explicit initialise step as the first act of every load path (both `applyStateJson` and `state_load`, closing B183 in the same change), plus a real `Init` patch in the factory bank — **there is none today**, 44 factory patches and not one of them is Init. **BUILT 2026-09-21 → PR #709** (verify full exit 0 on `cbdf1ce`): `initState` is the first act of both load paths, closing B183 in the same change; `docs/presets/factory/init/INIT - Init.json` exists — generated from an empty parameter table, so it is the shell's own defaults written by the shell's own writer — and is the bank's 41st patch. The gate is the one that would have caught the human's report: turn ON something no preset names, load a preset, and assert the instrument is byte-identical to loading that preset on a FRESH instance. That single assertion covers every parameter, every chunk and every future module at once, and it must be RED without the initialise step (the factory bank names every key, so a bank-only corpus will NOT distinguish them — L0059's exact trap, and the reason the B181 criterion passed on the unfixed binary). Sequenced after PR #705 merges: it edits the same state-chunk region. | § B181 · § B183 · § B186 · § L0059 |
| B190 | **Make a file's claim about its own place in the system CHECKABLE, and trigger the auditor on merges rather than days** (lead proposal 2026-09-20, answering the human's "Do you propose a solution to the gate issue?" after three stale headers surfaced in one day). The three had one shape: each stated the file's RELATIONSHIP to the rest of the system — `undo_check.cpp` "STANDALONE AND UNWIRED" while wired at `verify:239`; `subosc_core.h` "NOT wired into the shell, NO ids, NO routing source row, NO GUI" two days after all four became false; a CMake comment citing a refusal that had been replaced. Relationships are exactly what a tool can compute, so the rule to draw is: **a relationship is never written in prose when it can be declared and checked.** THREE LAYERS, and only two are mechanizable. **(1) A two-way wiring field.** Today only `UNWIRED: <reason>` is declarable. Add `WIRED: <where>`, require exactly one of the two in every `tools/*_check`, and have `test_table_check` CROSS-CHECK the declaration against `verify`'s own text — a file claiming unwired while wired then goes red instead of lying. 56 files, one line each, mechanical, strictly strengthening. **(2) The same trick for cores.** A core header's STATUS uses a fixed vocabulary (`CORE-ONLY` / `SHIPPED (ids …, source row …)`) and a check asserts it against the shell: does the shell reference the type, does it own a block. Catches `subosc_core.h`'s case; there are seven cores to cover. **(3) The rest is free prose and cannot be gated** — that is the auditor's charter already ("comments that describe a previous shape of the code"). The real failure there is TIMING: all three appeared within a day of the code changing, and the auditor cannot run again until 2026-09-26 under the seven-day rule — while **39 PRs merged in the 31 hours since the last audit**. Cadence by days is wrong for a repo moving this fast; trigger on merge count instead (25 merges or 7 days, whichever first), which also makes the trigger a fact about the repo rather than about the calendar. **LAYER 1 BUILT 2026-09-21 → PR #712:** all 56 check files carry exactly one line-anchored `WIRED: <where>` or `UNWIRED: <reason>`, cross-checked against `./verify`'s own text IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, with planted controls both ways AND a per-run `selftest()` that catches the detector itself going blind — the lesson from the ink detector that scored a blank canvas. `subosc_check.mjs`'s lying marker was caught BY THE NEW RULE rather than by hand, which is the only evidence that matters for a rule of this kind. TWO BOUNDARIES THE LAYER DOES NOT COVER, both stated rather than hidden: the cross-check verifies the NAME and not the TARGET, so a file declaring `WIRED: ./verify fast` that actually runs in `full()` passes — `morphlayout_check.cpp` was exactly that and was corrected by hand; parsing the `fast()`/`full()` bounds is easy and whether the gate should is the human's. And the rule inherits the old file-name boundary, so `cpu_check` and `alias_check` (built from `measure_*.cpp`) sit outside it, each carrying a header line anyway. Layer 3 is a change to CLAUDE.md §Domain's cadence rule and to the kit's proposed `/wakeup` step (autonomous brief hypersaw-003), so it wants the human's nod before it propagates. | § ADR-179 · § ADR-180 · § B159 |
| B186 | **A history-fidelity gauntlet, and the preset-reference bug the human hit** (human 2026-09-20: "I think I ran into a history bug. It has to do with references to loaded presets … make arbitrary changes to parameters, check if the history recorded them, step back to arbitrary points and branch, testing every node and then jumping back to parallel branches and making sure nothing has changed. One of the crucial steps to be tested rigorously is: loading global and corner presets. I seem to have experienced a bug where loading a different preset on a second branch switched the original branch over to the new preset and made the changes on top of it instead of on top of the initial preset"). **The deliverable is the GAUNTLET first, the diagnosis second, the fix third** — the agent is told not to start from a theory. A randomised SEEDED regime driving the real plugin through the CLAP factory: arbitrary edits recorded correctly (reusing ADR-160's calibrated zero-nodes-from-automation control rather than writing a second one), repeated step-back-and-branch to build a tree with real depth AND breadth, every node byte-identical whichever node you arrive from, and the property the human's bug violates stated as a pair rule — visiting a, then b, then a must land on a's exact stored state, and visiting b must never mutate what a stores. Global and corner preset loads are first-class steps in the random sequence, with at least two distinct presets so 'switched to the other preset' is expressible. Every row carries a must-fail control, and the plant is a version that shares the state pointer across branches; **L0059 is cited in the brief** — the lead wrote an acceptance criterion last week that passed on the unfixed binary, so a green here is worth nothing until each row is shown to fire. **WHAT THE LEAD ESTABLISHED BEFORE DISPATCHING, so the agent weighs it without being led:** a global preset load DOES mark exactly one node (`undoMark("load")`, `src/hypersaw_clap.cpp` ~5988) and a corner load marks through `undoMarkCorner` (~5465), so loads are recorded; a restore replays through `applyStateJson` (~5785), which CHANGED two days ago under B181 note 6 (an absent key now restores its default instead of being skipped) and is therefore in scope as either the fix or a new cause; and — the fact most likely to matter — **the GLOBAL preset's NAME is not shell state at all** (B174 specced, unbuilt), while corner names are and ride the morph chunk. So the interface's idea of which preset is loaded is GUI-local and appears in no snapshot. That makes two different failures possible, and only one is visible to the human: the VALUES being rebased onto the new preset, or the values being right while the displayed NAME follows the last load. The brief requires the agent to report state separately from display, and forbids building B174 here if that is the answer. **BUILT 2026-09-20 → PR #703** (verify full exit 0 on `8552fb6` read from `.harness/last-verify.json`; leak gate clean): a seeded layer-3 gauntlet inside `undo_check` (extended rather than siblinged, since that file is already wired) driving the real plugin through arbitrary edits, global- and corner-preset loads, step-backs and undo/redo, then asserting for EVERY ORDERED PAIR (a, b) that a → b → a lands on a's exact stored state and that visiting b never mutates what a stores. One templated sweep, THREE backends: the shell, plus two model histories built to be wrong (a shared buffer, a cross-branch write, navigation-that-records) — each must turn its row red, so the sweep is proven unable to pass by construction. Deterministic: seed printed and overridable, repeat runs byte-identical, 120 seeds green. **THE REPORTED BUG IS NOT IN THE STATE.** The literal scenario (load X, edit, step back, branch, load Y, return) plus 120 seeds show no cross-branch contamination and every node restores byte-identically. What the human saw is the DISPLAY: the global preset's name is not shell state, so no snapshot can carry it and the interface shows whatever was loaded last regardless of branch. That is B174's, now dispatched with this diagnosis folded in. **ONE DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED HERE:** a corner preset's name could be LOST from history when a GUI frame landed between the load and the naming, because `setCornerName` only amended a PENDING mark — shown red on the pre-fix binary (three rows) with a detector-reads-zero control. **THREE MORE FOUND, REPORTED NOT FIXED — two of them lose user data on ORDINARY preset loads, not only in history:** (i) id 1045 `o1.tilt` is clamped to 1 by the `toneTilt` alias, whose declared range differs (`swarm_core.h` 1438/1443) — B187; (ii) a state load that must MOVE COMB between slots loses it entirely (the fade shadow plus the singleton cap, `fx_rack.h:270`/`292` + `hypersaw_clap.cpp:6664`) — B188; both sit behind gauntlet exclusions that go RED when fixed, so the exclusions cannot rot, and each has a control proving the probe is not simply calling everything broken (id 45 round-trips; the same relocation with uncapped Notch round-trips). (iii) `undoGoTo` clears `undoPending` after `undoService()` early-returns on an undrained queue, so a mark taken while nothing drains is DISCARDED rather than collapsing into the next node, contrary to that function's own comment — fixing it needs a main-thread way to know the queue drained, which is an RT-discipline call for the human (B189). The stale `STANDALONE AND UNWIRED` header corrected. Deliberately out of scope and offered: the gauntlet stays under the 200-node cap (eviction remains layer 1's subject) and never uses the CLAP chunk transport. ALSO IN SCOPE, found by the lead while reading the seam: `tools/undo_check.cpp`'s header claims "STANDALONE AND UNWIRED. Not run by ./verify" and it has been WIRED at `verify:239` since 2026-09-13. **`test_table_check`'s wired-or-explained rule did not catch it**, because the rule looks for an `UNWIRED:` marker and this is prose asserting the opposite — a gate that reads markers cannot see a sentence that lies. Third stale header in one day (the sub core's STATUS block and a CMake comment were the other two, both fixed in #701); worth watching as a class rather than three incidents. | § ADR-160 · § B84 · § B174 · § B181 · § L0059 |

This NARROWS the 2026-08-21 placement, which committed all three phase-domain axes to the Saw shape section on OSC because they share one aliasing budget. **Withdrawn: Axis 2 phase-warp (formant), Axis 3 ripple, Axis 4 windowed carrier (formant).** Kept: **Axis 1 — hard sync**, whose controls in `docs/design/shape-lab.html` (~505) are `sync ratio` 1–8, `spread` 0–4, `← coupling` −1..1, `snap to int`, and the `chain order` select. | B180 | **Pitch becomes an ORDINARY mod destination (±48 st, any source, more than one) — and the gain envelopes become routable per oscillator** (human 2026-09-20, after looking at the per-oscillator Envelope panel: "It doesn't make any sense to me that ENV1 is some sort of maximum of both oscillators; what are these controls controlling?" and "there should be two pitch envelopes, or pitch should just be smoothly mappable to envelopes/LFOs on the mod matrix with a ±48 semitone range. That may be preferable to dedicated pitch envelopes"). **WHAT THE CODE SAYS (lead, 2026-09-20).** (1) The OSC Envelope panel controls that oscillator's AMPLITUDE over time — its loudness contour — per oscillator (19–22 / 1019–1022), each with its own per-voice mode (`voiceEnv`) and its own Onset & Scatter. Nothing is wrong with them. The mismatch is one level up: the matrix does NOT offer 'OSC 1's envelope' and 'OSC 2's envelope' as sources; it offers ONE derived source, `envMax`, the running maximum across every enabled oscillator's voices, and its comment says it 'stays' that way — it predates the per-oscillator split and was never revisited. (2) Pitch IS already a destination (`kModDestPitch`, a synthetic dest since pitch is not a CLAP parameter) but a CRIPPLED one: exactly ONE route, its source HARDWIRED to slot 1 (`mod.addRoute(1, kModDestPitch, …)`), and both `modSetSource` and `modSetPolarity` REFUSE any synthetic destination by design (ADR-135: knob 161 'owns that route's whole meaning', so a second author of the semitone offset is refused). Depth is param 161, ±48 st, persisted as a parameter rather than in the routes chunk. The route is `kGlobal` — one pitch path for both oscillators. **LEAD RECOMMENDS THE HUMAN'S SECOND OPTION, strongly:** make pitch an ordinary destination — any source, several routes at once, ±48 st each — rather than adding a second dedicated pitch envelope. It DELETES a special case instead of duplicating one, and 'two pitch envelopes' then falls out for free (route two envelopes at it), as does pitch from an LFO, a macro, velocity or ORBITAL. **ADR-135's real insight survives untouched:** it observed that a pitch envelope wants SUSTAIN 0 so pitch returns to base while the note holds, unlike an amp envelope sustaining at 1 (measured: depth +12 reads 390 Hz in the attack window and exactly 220.0 Hz in the held sustain). That is an argument for an envelope with its OWN ADSR — which ENV 3/4 already are — not for hardwiring one to pitch. **WHAT IT COSTS, stated before anyone says yes:** ADR-135 is overturned in part and needs an amendment; param 161 is saved state, so it either becomes the default pitch route's depth (compatibility preserved, the likely answer) or retires with a migration; pitch is applied per-VOICE rather than through the generic `base + delta·span` path, so a generic pitch route uses the per-voice application and its existing smoother; and the open sub-question is whether pitch destinations become PER-OSCILLATOR (OSC 1 pitch / OSC 2 pitch, which is literally what 'two pitch envelopes' asks for) or stay one global pitch path — the lead leans per-oscillator, since the human's whole complaint is that per-oscillator things are being collapsed. **COMPANION, small:** add `Gain ENV OSC 1` and `Gain ENV OSC 2` as real sources on the last two free slots (22, 23 of `kMaxSources` 24), so the source list matches the controls; `envMax` stays as its own source, renamed per B179. After this the source array is FULL and the cap must grow for anything further — say so at the constant. Not built: the human asked a question and gave an opinion, so this is the assessment and the ruling request, not a dispatch. | § ADR-135 · § B179 · § B134 · § B70 |
| B179 | **The envelope vocabulary is backwards — rename so the general-purpose pair is ENV 1/2 and the engine's own envelopes say what they are** (human 2026-09-20, on being told ENV 1 and ENV 2 are not what their names suggest: "we should just call the first editable ENVs on the MOD page 'ENV 1' & 'ENV 2' and call the other ones something else ('Gain ENV OSC 1', 'Pitch ENV OSC 2' etc.)"). The complaint is exactly right: today the two numbered ENV 1 / ENV 2 are the ones you CANNOT edit as envelopes (slot 0 is a read-only observation, slot 1 is the pitch envelope), while the actual general-purpose pair is numbered 3 and 4. The numbering advertises a series that does not exist. **THE HUMAN'S MODEL, CHECKED (lead, 2026-09-20):** right about the gain envelopes — there are TWO, per-oscillator (19–22 and 1019–1022), each with its own per-voice mode (`voiceEnv` 94/1094) and its own Onset & Scatter (91/93/95 + twins). WRONG about the pitch envelope — there is ONE, GLOBAL (162–165, depth 161), not one per oscillator. So the instrument has FIVE envelopes, not six: two gain, one pitch, two general-purpose. A name like 'Pitch ENV OSC 2' would invent a second pitch envelope. **WHY THE RENAME IS SAFE, and what must not move:** mod-source names are GUI-only presentation; parameter LABELS are host-visible but CLAP binds automation to the stable id, so a relabelled lane keeps its automation and merely displays a new name; the parameter KEYS (`env3A`…) are the saved-patch wire format and DO NOT MOVE — which leaves the deliberate wart that key `env3A` carries the label 'ENV 1 Attack', to be documented at the rows with that reason. Mod-source SLOT INDICES are frozen in the `modroutes` chunk (`src:dest:depth:pol;`), so this is a rename and NEVER a renumber: slot 20 keeps being slot 20 while displaying 'ENV 1', and every saved route stays correct — an old patch that routed slot 0 now reads 'Gain ENV', which is the correction the rename exists to make. **THE TABLE:** slot 20 `ENV 3` → **ENV 1**; slot 21 `ENV 4` → **ENV 2**; slot 0 `ENV 1` → **Gain ENV (loudest voice)** — NOT 'Gain ENV OSC 1', because it is the maximum across every ENABLED oscillator's gain envelope, not one oscillator's; slot 1 `ENV 2` → **Pitch ENV**. Params 281–288 relabel to `ENV 1/2 Attack…`; the MOD page's cluster titles, B177's visuals and B178's warnings follow. **WHAT THE HUMAN'S MODEL EXPECTS AND THE BUILD DOES NOT HAVE:** a per-oscillator gain-envelope source. Today only the max of both is routable. Slots **22 and 23 are the last two free** of `kMaxSources` 24, so adding `Gain ENV OSC 1` / `Gain ENV OSC 2` is two source writes and fills the array — after that the cap must grow. Offered, not built: the human rules. **B179's dispatch also carries the two layout defects B176 exposed** (the MOD page's multi-column flow breaking the ENV 3/4 and LFO 1/2 reading order, and the SUB panel sitting in a page sized for the swarm), since all three edit the same file. SEQUENCING: edits `src/gui/gui2.html`, `src/param_presentation.tsv` and `kParams`, all in flight under B176/B177/B178 — dispatch after PR #695 merges. | § B171 · § B178 · § ADR-135 · § B134 |

| B178 | **ENV 1 and ENV 2 on the MOD page as proxy controls, with warnings — and the human's premise corrected** (human 2026-09-20: "envelopes 1 & 2 should be represented on the MOD page with proxy controls and a warning that they control the gain of OSCs 1 and 2 respectively"). **THE PREMISE IS FALSE FOR BOTH AND THE LEAD CORRECTED IT BEFORE BUILDING** (verified in the shell the same day): ENV 1 (mod slot 0) is `envMax`, the maximum amp-envelope level across every voice of every ENABLED oscillator, and it has NO parameters of its own; ENV 2 (mod slot 1) is a dedicated per-note-slot ADSR with its own params 162–165 whose OTHER consumer is the pitch envelope at depth 161. | B174 | **The global preset persists across a GUI reload, with an asterisk when the patch has drifted from it** (human 2026-09-20: "I would like for the global preset to persist when you reload the GUI, like the corner presets do (if you've loaded a preset) — and it should have an asterisk if you've edited the patch without saving"). The human names the right model: the CORNER presets already do this and the global preset MIRRORS that trio rather than inventing a second mechanism. How corners do it (B122, `src/gui/gui2.html` ~2691-2790): the loaded NAME goes to the SHELL (`hzMorphCornerName`) so it lives in the patch chunk and survives a GUI reload, a save and an undo; the GUI reads names back from the shell (`hzMorphCornerNames`) rather than remembering them, because localStorage is unavailable under the plugin's opaque origin (ADR-105 A2); and the asterisk is THE SHELL'S OWN ANSWER to "would applying this preset change it?" (`hzMorphCornerDirty`), so dirty means one thing and cannot disagree with a load. Build the same three for the global patch: the name stored in the state chunk beside the corner names (append-only; absent reads empty, every existing patch bit-inert), a binding to read it back, and a dirty predicate reusing the corner comparison rather than a second copy. GUI: `#presetName` (~1020) shows the loaded name on reload and carries the existing `.cdirty` asterisk with the corner row's tooltip wording; saving clears it, loading sets both. **DISPATCHED 2026-09-20** (branch `global-preset-name`) once B186's gauntlet confirmed this row owns the human's reported bug: the state is correct and the DISPLAY is not, because no snapshot can carry a name the shell never holds. The brief folds in the defect #703 just fixed — a corner name could be lost when a GUI frame landed between the load and the naming, since only a PENDING mark was amended — and requires the node representing a load to already carry the name, with no window in which a mark can be taken without it. History is part of the acceptance, not an afterthought: a row expressing the human's exact branch scenario at the DISPLAY level (first branch must report X, not Y) must be RED before the change. **BUILT 2026-09-20 → PR #705** (verify full exit 0 on `73d8ecc` per `.harness/last-verify.json`; leak gate clean; 22 new rows in `undo_check`): `Plugin::presetName` rides BOTH the JSON chunk and the HOST chunk (so the name survives reopening the project, not just reloading the interface) and is written ONLY when non-empty, leaving every existing patch and session bit-inert; the GUI reads it back on the same 500 ms poll that reads the corner names rather than remembering it; the asterisk is the shell's own `presetMatches` answer. **THE NAMING WINDOW #703 FOUND IS CLOSED BY CONSTRUCTION, not by care:** the name is an ARGUMENT to `applyStateJson`, set before that function's own `undoMark`, so the state `undoService` snapshots already carries it — there is no instant at which a mark can be taken without the name. An empty argument defers to the patch's own key, which is how a restore recovers its branch's name. **THE HUMAN'S BUG IS NOW A TEST THAT WAS RED.** Removing the single `stateJson` line that emits the name reproduces the pre-B174 world, and six rows go red including the two that matter: `on the Y branch the patch reports Grackle` and `back on the FIRST branch the patch reports Squids, NOT Grackle`. What could NOT be shared, stated honestly by the agent: `presetMatches` could not reuse `cornerMatches` because that comparison's whole body is the morph slot array and the ADR-159 remap while a global patch is a parameter key set — so what is shared is the LAW (one `jsonNumber` reader of the absent-key rule, so the loader and the dirty predicate cannot drift), not the code. **MERGE ORDER MATTERS: #703 and #705 both rewrite `tools/undo_check.cpp` and CONFLICT** (`git merge-tree` confirms, one conflict, that file only) — merge #703 first, then #705; the lead resolves the header paragraph and the `main()` call list. THREE THINGS FOR THE HUMAN: (i) a SAVE marks no history node (it changes no values), so undoing across a save shows the older name — deliberate, and the alternative puts non-sonic nodes in history; (ii) the asterisk is a PARAMETER comparison and corners keep their own, so a corner edit does not raise the global one; (iii) **`presetMatches` reads permanently dirty for any parameter the loader clamps — which is exactly B187's `o1.tilt` alias clamp**, so a player loading such a preset sees a spurious asterisk until B187 is fixed; the oracle's own patches are taken to a load/save fixed point so these rows do not depend on that defect. That gives B187 a second visible symptom and raises it. Ratified: the acceptance screenshot committed to `docs/img/` (the repo's screenshot home, though outside the brief's file list) and the stale-header sentence corrected in passing. ACCEPTANCE: verify full green; load a preset, reload the GUI, the name is still shown; edit a parameter and the asterisk appears; save and it clears; a patch with no stored name loads unchanged with `state_check`/`statefix_check`/`bank_check` green; the name round-trips through the chunk. | § B122 · § ADR-105 |

ACCEPTANCE: (1) `src/undo_tree.h` — a pure, framework-free `UndoTree`: preallocated ring of `kUndoCap = 200` nodes `{parent, label, json, tick}`, no allocation after construction; a full ring evicts the OLDEST node and re-parents its children to its parent (a root's children become roots — a forest is legal); `current` node index; `push(label, json)` creates a child of `current` and moves `current` to it, and is a no-op when `json == current.json`; `undo()` moves to parent, `redo()` to the most recently CREATED child of current (the branch last taken), `restore(i)` moves `current` to any live node (navigation — no node is created; the next push forks from there). The audio thread touches nothing but is untouched: the mark is a main-thread act, the drain check is two atomic loads. (4) Restore = `applyStateJson(node.json)` and `current = node`; a restore is bit-identical: `stateJson()` after the queue drains equals `node.json` (the check asserts it through `tests/state_fixtures/`). (5) History is IN-MEMORY for 1.0 — never in the host chunk (`getStateInformation` unchanged, B43(b)); app-support persistence is a follow-up flag, not built. (6) GUI: a HISTORY page (`pg-HIST`, a page button beside the others) renders the tree as depth columns with the current node highlighted, any node one click to restore, Undo/Redo buttons, and Cmd/Ctrl+Z / Shift+Cmd/Ctrl+Z while the editor has focus; binds `hzUndoTree()` → `{cur, nodes:[{i,parent,label,tick}]}`, `hzUndoRestore(i)`, `hzUndo()`, `hzRedo()`. (7) `tools/undo_check.cpp`, standalone and unwired: ring eviction + re-parent, fork-on-restore, undo/redo path, dedup, the 200 cap, restore bit-identical through the fixture corpus, and the CONTROL: 500 host param events + 50 automation-shaped writes produce ZERO nodes. **Original outline** (human 2026-08-29: *"I want all my plugins to have a tree-based undo history... so forking history paths aren't lost"*). Instrument-level build: snapshot = the existing stateJson (provenance included), tree nodes on every gesture-end/preset-load, History tab renders the tree and any node is one click to restore (a restore from an old node FORKS — that is the point). | B66 | **Retrigger + roundness can CLICK** (human 2026-08-27, heard in use). Two candidate mechanisms, both concrete, and a probe that discriminates. **(a) The stale-rnd step:** `rnd[]` (per-voice roundness weights) is computed only in `controlTick`, which runs every `kTick = 16` samples on a GLOBAL tick counter -- so a retriggered note renders up to 15 samples with the PREVIOUS state's weights, then steps to the new ones mid-waveform. **(b) The reset-phase step:** retrigger resets phase while the profile shape (`sawShapeTab`) need not be zero at ph=0 the way the polyBLEP saw is, so a voice with residual envelope (steal, fast repress) jumps to a nonzero waveform value at reset -- amplitude scales with `rnd[i]`, which is why roundness makes it audible. **The discriminating probe:** render a retrigger with round high and measure the first-32-sample discontinuity (i) as shipped, (ii) with rnd frozen across the retrigger (isolates a), (iii) with round = 0 (isolates b). If (b) dominates, the fix is the ADR-083 shape -- a short declick ramp at retrigger, or starting the shaped blend from the phase the saw actually resets to; if (a), compute `rnd[]` at noteOn as well as at the tick | § ADR-094 · § ADR-083 |

| B64 | **PITCH ENVELOPE — wanted ASAP** (human 2026-08-27). **There is none today:** no `pitchEnv`/`penv` anywhere in the shell or the core, so this is a build rather than an exposure. **The shape to mirror is right beside it.** The amp envelope is ids 19-22 (attack/decay/sustain/release, seconds, ADR-021 — *"defaults reproduce the reference AR bit-exactly"*), and `Voice` already carries `env` per note, so a second per-voice envelope is the same state pattern in the same struct rather than new architecture. **Three decisions the build needs, none of them obvious.** (a) **Depth and polarity** — a pitch envelope wants a bipolar DEPTH in semitones (so it can dive as well as rise), which is a separate param from the four times; the ADR-056 / ADR-133 bipolar-superset pattern applies (default 0 = inert = every golden byte-identical). (b) **Where it sums** — the shell already folds four transposition sources into ONE live tune factor (ADR-027: semi + fine + bend + octave), so the pitch envelope should join THAT sum rather than become a fifth independent path, or two of them will fight over who owns pitch. (c) **Whether it is per-note or global.** Per B34's scope tiering this is **Tier 1, free** — it is a scalar read inside the per-voice tick and `Voice` already has the state — which is also the musically right answer, since a pitch envelope that is not per-note cannot do the thing it is for (each note diving from its own start pitch). **Parity:** default depth 0 makes the whole feature inert, so this is a parity-safe superset and no golden moves | § ADR-021 · § ADR-027 · § B34 |
| B65 | **The silent oscillator's parameters: junk, hiding place, or destination?** (human 2026-08-27, observed from ADR-123's ramp in use). **The observation, which is correct.** When corner A has an oscillator OFF and corner B has it ON, ADR-123 now fades it in across the morph — but its *other* parameters morph independently, and in corner A they hold whatever was left there while it was silent: init defaults, or settings nobody ever heard and therefore never tuned. So the oscillator becomes **audible before its character arrives**, fading in wearing corner A's unauthored settings and only gradually acquiring B's. **The human names both readings, and both are right.** As a defect: the fade-in sounds like the wrong instrument. As a feature: those silent settings are a **hiding place** — deliberately author something in the silent oscillator and it emerges during the morph, which is a genuinely novel gesture and exactly the kind of thing this morph field exists to make possible. They are mutually exclusive, which is why the proposal is a **toggle** rather than a fix. **THE MACHINERY IS HALF-BUILT ALREADY, which nobody noticed.** ADR-108's `depLiveInCorner` exists and `morphStep` already calls it: *"if this parameter's enabling condition is false IN THE CORNER THAT WON IT, the flip would be a no-op... Hold instead."* That is the same problem — a parameter drawn from a corner where it could not be heard — solved one way. **It does not fire here for one reason: no per-oscillator parameter declares a dependency on `enable`** (checked: zero rows in the presentation table have `depends: enable=...`). Declaring them would give the HOLD behaviour immediately, for free. **Three candidate behaviours, and the toggle should choose between them explicitly:** (1) **AUTHOR** (today) — the silent corner's values are real and morph normally; the hiding place works; the fade-in can sound wrong. (2) **HOLD** (ADR-108's existing answer, one TSV column away) — a parameter whose corner has the oscillator off keeps its current value instead of taking that corner's; conservative, cheap, already implemented. (3) **ADOPT** (the human's proposal) — the silent oscillator takes the parameters of the corner it is heading toward, so it fades in already sounding like its destination. **THE HARD PART OF (3), and the reason it is not simply better:** *"the corner it is morphing into"* is not well-defined. The pad is 2-D with four corners and no from/to — there are only weights. At (0.4, 0.6) an oscillator is heading toward all four at once. So ADOPT needs a rule: the highest-weight corner? the nearest corner where the oscillator is ON? the weighted average of only the ON corners? Each gives a different sound and the last is probably the musical one, but it is a design decision that a 1-D A-to-B mental model hides. **RULED 2026-08-27: the human ratified the weighted-average-of-ON-corners rule** (*"Yeah, I think weighted average of only the on corners sounds right"*), so ADOPT's rule is settled and the build order stands: declare the dependencies first (HOLD for free), then ADOPT as the toggle's third position. Note this generalises past oscillators: FX slot params in a corner whose slot is Off have the identical problem, so whatever rule is chosen should be stated in terms of *inaudible parameters*, not *silent oscillators* | § ADR-108 · § ADR-123 · § ADR-131 |
| B63 | **An OTT-style band compressor, and how much of it to build at once** (human 2026-08-27: *"I want to make sure there is an OTT effect (maybe a special compressor setting), even if we don't add a fully modifiable multi-band compressor right off the bat"*). **Assessment: the full thing is more buildable than it looks, because both halves already exist in this repo.** OTT is multiband **upward AND downward** compression -- the upward half is what makes it sound like OTT rather than like a compressor, and it is the half most clones get wrong by omitting. What we have: `filter_core.h` carries a **TPT/ZDF state-variable filter**, which is exactly the crossover a 3-band split needs (and B45 already lists generalising it as the filter-bank's item 1); and `fx_rack.h`'s `Comp` slot is a working comp+limiter with an envelope follower. A 3-band OTT is therefore *crossover + three instances of dynamics we already own*, not a green-field DSP build. **The honest cost is not the DSP, it is the SURFACE — and my first framing of that was misleading, corrected here 2026-08-27.** I wrote "~21 parameters against the 8-id block" as though the block were a wall. It is not: **8 was a stride I chose in ADR-131, and id space is not scarce** — 232..999 is unallocated (768 ids) with the routing block reserved separately at 10000+. Three things are actually true, and only the third is a ceiling. **(a) Ids are APPEND-ONLY, so the block cannot be WIDENED, only supplemented.** A saved patch stores the integer, so 200..231 cannot be renumbered to make room; a 21-param module would take a second block elsewhere, and its params would then not sit contiguously with its slot's other seven — which breaks ADR-131's `slot = (id-200)/8` arithmetic dispatch and forces a second rule. That is a real cost and it is structural, not cosmetic. **(b) Automation-lane clutter is the cost the PLAYER pays.** 4 slots x 21 = **84 more parameters** in every host's automation list, on top of 188 declared today. That is the reason to stage exposure, and it has nothing to do with running out of anything. **(c) The one hard ceiling is `morph_core.h`'s `kMaxParams = 512`**, against a morphIds set currently around 269. 84 more is comfortably inside; a fully-parameterised roster of many modules would not be, so the ceiling is worth knowing before the filter bank and STATION both land. **So the sequencing question is not id allocation at all — it is whether a player can navigate 84 more automation lanes before a per-slot page design exists to organise them.** **Recommended shape: build the DSP whole, expose it in two stages.** Stage 1 ships ONE macro -- *depth* -- over fixed, tuned band settings, which is what the famous preset actually is and what the human asked for; the full parameter set lands with the per-slot pages (B50's rework), where a 21-param slot page has somewhere to live. Building the DSP once avoids the trap of shipping a fixed-ratio approximation and then rewriting it. **Do NOT start before B50's slot-contract ruling:** a multiband compressor is exactly the module that wants block processing for its detectors, so it is affected by the per-sample fork more than any other slot type | § B45 · § B50 · § ADR-131 |
| B62 | **Morph FLIP TIMING — the reference has it and the port never did** (human 2026-08-27: *"I would like to reintroduce the morph glide modes, including tempo and note sync settings"*). **"Reintroduce" is the wrong word and the distinction matters: nothing was removed.** `docs/design/quantum-morph-lab.html` -- which morph_core.h names as its reference, and which ADR-003 makes the spec -- carries a **Flip timing** control with two values, *Immediate* and *Next note*. The C++ port implemented neither; it is always Immediate. That guard is the whole design and should be ported with it, or moving the pad in silence would appear to do nothing. **Build shape:** a `morphTiming` param (0 immediate, 1 next note, default 0 = today's behaviour = parity-safe), a pending assignment held beside `morphCur`, and a commit hook on note-on. Note the interaction with ADR-123: an osc enable that flips on the next note now also has a level ramp, so the ramp should start AT the commit rather than at the pad move. **CORRECTED 2026-08-27 -- I called tempo sync "invention" and the human corrected it: *"I had always intended tempo sync to be an option along with Hz and next note."* So the design is a FOUR-VALUE mode, not a port plus an invention: continuous (today's behaviour, the default), free (Hz), sync, and next note.** That reframing matters because **the codebase already ships this exact trio and the machinery to resolve it.** `kQTimeModeLabels[] = {"continuous", "free (Hz)", "sync"}` (id 146) with `bendQTimeHz` (147) and `bendQTimeSync` (148), resolved by `resolveQTimeMs()`: mode 1 returns `1000/Hz`, mode 2 returns `1000 / ((bpm/60) * grid)` with the host's tempo and a guard against an absent transport handing the gate an infinity. **Morph timing should reuse the vocabulary AND the shape** -- `morphTimeMode` / `morphTimeHz` / `morphTimeSync` mirroring 146/147/148, and a `resolveMorphPeriod()` that is `resolveQTimeMs()` with a different member set. A player who has learned Step Timing on the bend page then already knows this control, which is worth more than any cleverness available by designing it fresh. Only *next note* has no precedent in the shell -- and that one IS in the reference lab, with its held-notes guard | § ADR-104 · § ADR-123 · § ADR-133 · § ADR-003 |
| B60 | **SHIPPED 2026-08-27 (ADR-133)** — range -1..1, default 0, formula untouched; tilt measured exactly symmetric from the core's rnd[] (-1.000 / +1.000, flat at zero); parity 156/156. Original entry follows. **Round x Pitch becomes BIPOLAR — negative skews roundness to the LOW voices** (human 2026-08-27: *"I think round x pitch should be bipolar, with the other direction skewing the roundness to the low end voices instead of the high end"*). **Already a one-character change in the math, which is why this is a range decision rather than a DSP one.** `swarm_core.h` computes `s.rnd[i] = clamp(p.round * (1 + p.roundHi * (2*up - 1)))` where `up` is the voice's normalised position in the spread, so `2*up - 1` already runs -1..+1 across the swarm. At `roundHi > 0` the high voices round more; at `roundHi < 0` the SAME expression skews it to the low voices. The param is declared `{132, "roundHi", "Round x Pitch", 0, 1, 0}` -- the only thing preventing the requested behaviour is the lower bound. **The change is therefore: range 0..1 -> -1..1, default unchanged at 0.** **Parity-safe as a superset:** the default is 0, `(1 + 0*x) == 1`, and no golden sets roundHi, so every golden is byte-identical -- the same shape as ADR-056's bipolar onset lock, which widened a 0..1 knob to -1..1 for exactly this reason and is the precedent to follow. **Two things to check when building:** (a) the clamp already floors at 0, so a strongly negative roundHi drives the top voices to rnd = 0 rather than negative -- correct, but confirm the taper still feels smooth rather than hitting a wall partway; (b) the GUI knob must become BIPOLAR in its paint (`paintFill`'s `bip` test keys on `lo < 0 && hi > 0`, so it follows automatically once the range moves -- verify rather than assume). Presentation row and the knob's zero-at-centre behaviour come free from that test | § ADR-056 · § ADR-094 |
| B57 | **The silent spring — a mass-spring driven by note motion, as a MODULATOR** (human 2026-08-27: *"simulate the same mass-spring effect as in the inertial pitch bend settings, but use the vector between the inertia and the flat midi note as a modulator... regardless of whether pitch bend is active on the notes themselves"*). **The quantity already exists and is discarded.** `glide_core.h`'s spring integrator computes `vel += (w*w*(target - x) - 2*z*w*vel)*dt`, and **`target - x` IS the vector** -- the displacement of the simulated mass from the flat MIDI note, evaluated every control tick and thrown away. Exposing it is the feature. **A SECOND, SILENT SPRING, on the modulator page** (human's refinement): tapping the AUDIBLE traveller fails by construction, because when the lane's law is `off (instant)` x snaps to target and the displacement is permanently zero -- which is exactly the *"regardless of whether pitch bend is active"* case. So it is its own instance with its own stiffness/damping, running whether or not anything is audibly gliding, and its only output is modulation. It also **doubles as an alternative keytracking modulator** -- keytracking reads absolute pitch, this reads how far you just LEAPT, which is a different musical statement. **Follow-toggles** (follow pitch bend / note glide / MPE spring) let it lock to an existing lane instead of running free -- and each toggle is **visible only when the lane it follows is already active**, so the page never offers a control that would do nothing (the dead-control failure `gui_reach` exists to catch, applied at the GUI level). **Four decisions that shape the feel:** (a) **signed vs magnitude** -- signed means upward leaps modulate opposite to downward, magnitude means any large interval does the same thing; signed is rarer and probably the musical one; (b) **per-note** (human: "per-note suffices") -- see the scope tiering in B34: this is Tier 1, free, because it is a scalar read inside the per-voice tick; (c) **normalisation** -- an octave leap is 12x a semitone, so raw displacement swamps any destination without a reference interval; (d) **tap point** -- `x` is pre-quantise, the emitted value post; glide_core's own header notes spring + scale-quantise gives *"an overshooting autotune wobble"*, which the modulation would inherit if tapped after. **A second output for free:** `vel` sits beside `x` in the same struct -- the mass's VELOCITY is a different modulator with a different shape (displacement is largest the instant you leap and decays; velocity peaks mid-flight). **Blocked on B16/B23** -- there are no modulators at all yet. **PRIOR-ART flag before this reaches the README:** modulation driven by melodic INTERVAL SIZE with physical dynamics has no shipping example I can name -- key velocity, key tracking and envelopes are the usual three and none is this -- but that is an absence of knowledge, not a search; research it properly before claiming it | § B16 · § B23 · § B34 · § ADR-096 **REVIVED 2026-10-01 (human: "I appreciate you resurfacing the spring-displacement-as-mod-surface gap.
